question: How many products does Northwind Traders currently offer in each category? Return the CategoryID and the total number of products for each category, ordered by the total number of products in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Merchandising wants a quick summary of how Northwind's product catalog is distributed across categories. This will help identify which categories are over- or under-represented ahead of the next supplier negotiation cycle.
reference_sql: SELECT CategoryID, COUNT(ProductID) AS TotalProducts FROM Products GROUP BY CategoryID ORDER BY TotalProducts DESC;

question: How many orders has each customer placed? Return the CustomerID and the total number of orders, ordered by the total number of orders in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants a quick summary of customer engagement to identify the most active buyers. This will help the team prioritize outreach for the upcoming promotional campaign.
reference_sql: SELECT CustomerID, COUNT(OrderID) AS TotalOrders FROM Orders GROUP BY CustomerID ORDER BY TotalOrders DESC

question: Write a query that returns each shipper (identified by ShipVia) along with the total number of orders they handled, the average freight cost, the minimum freight cost, and the maximum freight cost. Only include shippers that have handled more than 100 orders. Order the results by average freight cost in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Logistics wants to evaluate shipper performance and cost efficiency across all completed orders. She needs a summary of freight statistics per shipper to identify which carriers are being used most and whether their costs are in line with expectations.
reference_sql: SELECT ShipVia, COUNT(OrderID) AS TotalOrders, ROUND(AVG(Freight), 2) AS AvgFreight, MIN(Freight) AS MinFreight, MAX(Freight) AS MaxFreight FROM Orders GROUP BY ShipVia HAVING COUNT(OrderID) > 100 ORDER BY AvgFreight DESC

question: For each shipper (ShipVia), calculate the total number of orders, the average freight cost, the minimum freight cost, and the maximum freight cost. Only include shippers that have handled more than 50 orders. Order the results by average freight cost in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Logistics wants to evaluate shipping carrier performance and cost patterns. She needs a summary of freight cost statistics per carrier to support upcoming contract renegotiations with shipping partners.
reference_sql: SELECT ShipVia, COUNT(OrderID) AS TotalOrders, ROUND(AVG(Freight), 2) AS AvgFreight, MIN(Freight) AS MinFreight, MAX(Freight) AS MaxFreight FROM Orders GROUP BY ShipVia HAVING COUNT(OrderID) > 50 ORDER BY AvgFreight DESC

question: For each year and month of order activity, calculate the total number of orders, total freight cost, average freight cost per order, and the cumulative (running) total freight cost ordered chronologically by year and month. Only include year-month combinations where the total freight exceeds the overall average monthly freight across all months. Return the year, month, order count, total freight, average freight, and running total freight.
business_context: The VP of Operations wants to identify high-freight months to better negotiate shipping contracts and plan logistics budgets. She specifically wants to see how freight costs accumulate over time, but only wants to focus on months that are above average in freight spend to avoid noise from slow periods.
reference_sql:
WITH monthly_freight AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS order_year,
        CAST(strftime('%m', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS order_month,
        COUNT(OrderID) AS total_orders,
        ROUND(SUM(Freight), 2) AS total_freight,
        ROUND(AVG(Freight), 2) AS avg_freight_per_order
    FROM Orders
    WHERE OrderDate IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY order_year, order_month
),
overall_avg AS (
    SELECT AVG(total_freight) AS overall_avg_monthly_freight
    FROM monthly_freight
)
SELECT
    mf.order_year,
    mf.order_month,
    mf.total_orders,
    mf.total_freight,
    mf.avg_freight_per_order,
    ROUND(SUM(mf.total_freight) OVER (ORDER BY mf.order_year, mf.order_month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS running_total_freight
FROM monthly_freight mf
CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
WHERE mf.total_freight > oa.overall_avg_monthly_freight
ORDER BY mf.order_year, mf.order_month

question: For each year and month, calculate the total freight cost, the number of orders shipped, the average freight per order, and the month-over-month percentage change in total freight cost. Only include months where at least 10 orders were shipped (i.e., ShippedDate is not null). Order the results by year and month ascending.
business_context: The Head of Logistics at Northwind Traders wants a detailed monthly freight cost report to identify shipping cost trends and flag months with unusual spikes or drops. She specifically needs the month-over-month percentage change so she can quickly spot anomalies without manually comparing rows.
reference_sql:
WITH monthly_freight AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(strftime('%Y', ShippedDate) AS INTEGER) AS ship_year,
        CAST(strftime('%m', ShippedDate) AS INTEGER) AS ship_month,
        COUNT(OrderID) AS orders_shipped,
        SUM(Freight) AS total_freight,
        ROUND(AVG(Freight), 2) AS avg_freight_per_order
    FROM Orders
    WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY ship_year, ship_month
    HAVING COUNT(OrderID) >= 10
),
with_lag AS (
    SELECT
        ship_year,
        ship_month,
        orders_shipped,
        total_freight,
        avg_freight_per_order,
        LAG(total_freight) OVER (ORDER BY ship_year, ship_month) AS prev_month_freight
    FROM monthly_freight
)
SELECT
    ship_year,
    ship_month,
    orders_shipped,
    ROUND(total_freight, 2) AS total_freight,
    avg_freight_per_order,
    CASE
        WHEN prev_month_freight IS NULL OR prev_month_freight = 0 THEN NULL
        ELSE ROUND(100.0 * (total_freight - prev_month_freight) / prev_month_freight, 2)
    END AS mom_freight_pct_change
FROM with_lag
ORDER BY ship_year, ship_month;

question: Find all customers who have placed more than 10 orders. Return the customer ID and their total number of orders, ordered by order count descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-frequency buyers to target for a VIP loyalty program. They need a list of customers who have placed more than 10 orders so the sales team can prioritize outreach.
reference_sql: SELECT CustomerID, COUNT(OrderID) AS TotalOrders FROM Orders GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(OrderID) > 10 ORDER BY TotalOrders DESC

question: Find all customers who have placed more than 10 orders. Return the CustomerID and the total number of orders they have placed, ordered by order count descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-frequency buyers for a new loyalty rewards program. She needs a list of customers who have placed more than 10 orders so the account management team can prioritize outreach.
reference_sql: SELECT CustomerID, COUNT(OrderID) AS TotalOrders FROM Orders GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(OrderID) > 10 ORDER BY TotalOrders DESC

question: Write a query to find all customers who have placed more than 10 orders in total. Return the customer's ID, company name, and their total number of orders, sorted by order count descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-frequency buyers for a VIP loyalty program. She needs a list of customers who have placed more than 10 orders so the account management team can reach out with exclusive wholesale pricing offers.
reference_sql: SELECT c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS TotalOrders FROM Customers c JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName HAVING COUNT(o.OrderID) > 10 ORDER BY TotalOrders DESC

question: Identify all customers who have placed more than 10 orders and whose average freight cost per order exceeds $50. Return the customer ID, company name, total number of orders, and average freight cost rounded to 2 decimal places.
business_context: The Head of Logistics has noticed that certain high-volume customers are generating disproportionate shipping costs. They want to identify customers who are both frequent buyers and costly to ship to, so the team can negotiate better shipping terms or freight surcharges for these accounts.
reference_sql: SELECT o.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS TotalOrders, ROUND(AVG(o.Freight), 2) AS AvgFreight FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID GROUP BY o.CustomerID, c.CompanyName HAVING COUNT(o.OrderID) > 10 AND AVG(o.Freight) > 50 ORDER BY AvgFreight DESC

question: Identify customers who have placed at least 5 orders and whose average order value (sum of UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount) per order, plus Freight) exceeds $500. For each such customer, return their CompanyName, total number of orders, average order value (rounded to 2 decimal places), and the total revenue they have generated. Order results by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-value, high-frequency customers for a new VIP loyalty program. Only customers who order frequently AND spend generously on average should qualify, so the team can prioritize outreach and offer exclusive pricing tiers.
reference_sql: WITH OrderValues AS ( SELECT o.OrderID, o.CustomerID, o.Freight, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS OrderLineTotal, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) + o.Freight AS OrderTotal FROM Orders o JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.CustomerID, o.Freight ) SELECT c.CompanyName, COUNT(ov.OrderID) AS TotalOrders, ROUND(AVG(ov.OrderTotal), 2) AS AvgOrderValue, ROUND(SUM(ov.OrderTotal), 2) AS TotalRevenue FROM OrderValues ov JOIN Customers c ON ov.CustomerID = c.CustomerID GROUP BY ov.CustomerID, c.CompanyName HAVING COUNT(ov.OrderID) >= 5 AND AVG(ov.OrderTotal) > 500 ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC

question: Identify customers who have placed at least 5 orders and whose average order value (sum of UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount) per order) exceeds $500. For each such customer, return their CompanyName, total number of orders, average order value rounded to 2 decimal places, and the total revenue they have generated. Order results by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-value, loyal customers for a new VIP program. Specifically, they need customers who order frequently (5+ orders) and consistently spend above $500 per order on average, so the account management team can prioritize outreach and tailor exclusive offers.
reference_sql:
WITH OrderValues AS (
    SELECT
        o.OrderID,
        o.CustomerID,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS OrderValue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.CustomerID
),
CustomerStats AS (
    SELECT
        CustomerID,
        COUNT(OrderID) AS TotalOrders,
        ROUND(AVG(OrderValue), 2) AS AvgOrderValue,
        ROUND(SUM(OrderValue), 2) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM OrderValues
    GROUP BY CustomerID
    HAVING COUNT(OrderID) >= 5
        AND AVG(OrderValue) > 500
)
SELECT
    c.CompanyName,
    cs.TotalOrders,
    cs.AvgOrderValue,
    cs.TotalRevenue
FROM CustomerStats cs
JOIN Customers c ON cs.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
ORDER BY cs.TotalRevenue DESC;

question: Using a CTE, calculate the total revenue (UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) for each customer and return the top 5 customers by total revenue, showing their CompanyName and total revenue rounded to 2 decimal places.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants a quick snapshot of Northwind's most valuable customers by total spend. She needs this formatted clearly for an executive presentation next week and wants to use a reusable query structure for future reporting.
reference_sql:
WITH CustomerRevenue AS (
    SELECT
        o.CustomerID,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    GROUP BY o.CustomerID
)
SELECT
    c.CompanyName,
    cr.TotalRevenue
FROM CustomerRevenue cr
JOIN Customers c ON cr.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
ORDER BY cr.TotalRevenue DESC
LIMIT 5;

question: Using a CTE, calculate the total revenue (UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) for each customer, then return only the customers whose total revenue exceeds $10,000. Display the CustomerID and their total revenue rounded to 2 decimal places, ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-value customers who have generated more than $10,000 in net revenue to prioritize them for a new loyalty program. She needs a clean list of these customers ranked by their contribution to overall revenue.
reference_sql:
WITH CustomerRevenue AS (
    SELECT
        o.CustomerID,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    GROUP BY o.CustomerID
)
SELECT CustomerID, TotalRevenue
FROM CustomerRevenue
WHERE TotalRevenue > 10000
ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC;

question: Using a CTE, calculate the total revenue (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)) per customer, then return only the customers whose total revenue exceeds the average total revenue across all customers. Include the customer's company name, country, and their total revenue, ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-value customers who spend above the average customer spend. This will inform a new tiered loyalty program and help the sales team prioritize account management efforts for Q3.
reference_sql:
WITH CustomerRevenue AS (
    SELECT
        c.CustomerID,
        c.CompanyName,
        c.Country,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Customers c
    JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, c.Country
)
SELECT
    CompanyName,
    Country,
    TotalRevenue
FROM CustomerRevenue
WHERE TotalRevenue > (SELECT AVG(TotalRevenue) FROM CustomerRevenue)
ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC

question: Using a CTE, calculate the total revenue (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)) generated by each product category. Then return only the categories whose total revenue exceeds the average category revenue across all categories. Display the category name and its total revenue, ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify which product categories are performing above average in terms of revenue contribution. This will help prioritize inventory investment and marketing efforts for the upcoming quarter.
reference_sql:
WITH category_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        c.CategoryName,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Categories c
    JOIN Products p ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
    GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName
)
SELECT
    CategoryName,
    ROUND(TotalRevenue, 2) AS TotalRevenue
FROM category_revenue
WHERE TotalRevenue > (SELECT AVG(TotalRevenue) FROM category_revenue)
ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC

question: For each product category, identify the top 2 customers (by total revenue) and calculate what percentage of that category's total revenue they represent. Include the category name, customer company name, their total spend in that category, and their revenue percentage share. Order results by category name and revenue percentage descending.
business_context: The VP of Sales wants to understand category-level revenue concentration risk. She suspects that for certain product categories, revenue is heavily dependent on just one or two key accounts, and wants a report showing the top 2 customers per category along with their share of that category's total revenue to inform retention strategy planning.
reference_sql:
WITH category_customer_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        c.CategoryID,
        c.CategoryName,
        o.CustomerID,
        cu.CompanyName,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS total_spend
    FROM Categories c
    JOIN Products p ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
    JOIN Orders o ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
    JOIN Customers cu ON o.CustomerID = cu.CustomerID
    GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName, o.CustomerID, cu.CompanyName
),
category_totals AS (
    SELECT
        CategoryID,
        SUM(total_spend) AS category_total_revenue
    FROM category_customer_revenue
    GROUP BY CategoryID
),
ranked_customers AS (
    SELECT
        ccr.CategoryName,
        ccr.CompanyName,
        ccr.total_spend,
        ct.category_total_revenue,
        ROUND(100.0 * ccr.total_spend / ct.category_total_revenue, 2) AS revenue_pct,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ccr.CategoryID ORDER BY ccr.total_spend DESC) AS rn
    FROM category_customer_revenue ccr
    JOIN category_totals ct ON ccr.CategoryID = ct.CategoryID
)
SELECT
    CategoryName,
    CompanyName,
    total_spend,
    revenue_pct
FROM ranked_customers
WHERE rn <= 2
ORDER BY CategoryName ASC, revenue_pct DESC

question: For each product category, identify the top 2 customers (by total revenue) and show how their spending compares to the category average customer spend. Return the category name, customer company name, the customer's total revenue for that category, the average revenue per customer in that category, and the percentage difference between the customer's spend and the category average. Round all monetary values to 2 decimal places.
business_context: The VP of Sales wants to understand which customers are driving outsized revenue within each product category. She needs to identify the top spenders per category and benchmark them against the typical customer in that same category, so the sales team can prioritize account management efforts and tailor promotions accordingly.
reference_sql:
WITH customer_category_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        c.CategoryID,
        cat.CategoryName,
        o.CustomerID,
        cu.CompanyName,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS total_revenue
    FROM "Order Details" od
    JOIN Orders o ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
    JOIN Products c ON od.ProductID = c.ProductID
    JOIN Categories cat ON c.CategoryID = cat.CategoryID
    JOIN Customers cu ON o.CustomerID = cu.CustomerID
    GROUP BY c.CategoryID, cat.CategoryName, o.CustomerID, cu.CompanyName
),
category_avg AS (
    SELECT
        CategoryID,
        ROUND(AVG(total_revenue), 2) AS avg_customer_revenue
    FROM customer_category_revenue
    GROUP BY CategoryID
),
ranked_customers AS (
    SELECT
        ccr.CategoryID,
        ccr.CategoryName,
        ccr.CustomerID,
        ccr.CompanyName,
        ccr.total_revenue,
        ca.avg_customer_revenue,
        ROUND((ccr.total_revenue - ca.avg_customer_revenue) / ca.avg_customer_revenue * 100, 2) AS pct_diff_from_avg,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ccr.CategoryID ORDER BY ccr.total_revenue DESC) AS revenue_rank
    FROM customer_category_revenue ccr
    JOIN category_avg ca ON ccr.CategoryID = ca.CategoryID
)
SELECT
    CategoryName,
    CompanyName,
    total_revenue,
    avg_customer_revenue,
    pct_diff_from_avg,
    revenue_rank
FROM ranked_customers
WHERE revenue_rank <= 2
ORDER BY CategoryName, revenue_rank;

question: Rank all products by their unit price from highest to lowest. Return the product name, unit price, and rank. Use RANK() so that products with the same price share the same rank.
business_context: The Head of Procurement wants a quick reference list showing how products compare in price relative to each other. They specifically want tied prices to share the same rank position so buyers can easily spot equally-priced items.
reference_sql: SELECT ProductName, UnitPrice, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY UnitPrice DESC) AS PriceRank FROM Products ORDER BY PriceRank;

question: Rank all products by their unit price from highest to lowest using RANK(). Return the product name, unit price, and their price rank. Include all products, even if they share the same price.
business_context: The Head of Procurement wants a quick reference list showing how products stack up against each other by price. She needs to identify which products sit at the top of the pricing hierarchy so the team can prioritize margin discussions with suppliers.
reference_sql: SELECT ProductName, UnitPrice, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY UnitPrice DESC) AS PriceRank FROM Products

question: For each product category, identify the top 2 best-selling products by total revenue (unit price × quantity, before discounts). Return the category name, product name, total revenue, and the rank within the category. If two products tie for the same rank, both should appear with the same rank value.
business_context: The Head of Merchandising wants to spotlight the star products in each category for the upcoming trade catalog. She needs to know which two products drive the most revenue per category so the marketing team can feature them prominently in promotional materials.
reference_sql: WITH product_revenue AS ( SELECT p.ProductID, p.ProductName, c.CategoryName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity) AS TotalRevenue FROM Products p JOIN Categories c ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID JOIN "Order Details" od ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName, c.CategoryName ), ranked_products AS ( SELECT CategoryName, ProductName, TotalRevenue, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY CategoryName ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC) AS RevenueRank FROM product_revenue ) SELECT CategoryName, ProductName, TotalRevenue, RevenueRank FROM ranked_products WHERE RevenueRank <= 2 ORDER BY CategoryName, RevenueRank

question: For each product category, identify the top 2 best-selling products by total revenue (unit price × quantity, before discounts). Return the category name, product name, total revenue, and the rank within its category. If two products tie in revenue, they should share the same rank.
business_context: The Head of Merchandising wants to spotlight the top-performing products in each category for an upcoming marketing campaign. They need a ranked list showing the two highest-grossing products per category so the team can prioritize promotional efforts accordingly.
reference_sql:
WITH ProductRevenue AS (
    SELECT
        c.CategoryName,
        p.ProductName,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Products p
    JOIN Categories c ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
    GROUP BY c.CategoryName, p.ProductName
),
RankedProducts AS (
    SELECT
        CategoryName,
        ProductName,
        TotalRevenue,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY CategoryName ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC) AS RevenueRank
    FROM ProductRevenue
)
SELECT
    CategoryName,
    ProductName,
    TotalRevenue,
    RevenueRank
FROM RankedProducts
WHERE RevenueRank <= 2
ORDER BY CategoryName, RevenueRank;

question: For each product category, identify the top 2 products by total revenue (unit price × quantity, accounting for discounts). If two products tie for the same rank within a category, both should appear. Return the category name, product name, total revenue rounded to 2 decimal places, and the rank within the category. Order results by category name and rank.
business_context: The VP of Merchandising wants a category-level view of our best-performing products to inform next quarter's procurement strategy. She specifically needs to see tied products both represented if they share a top-2 rank, so DENSE_RANK must be used rather than ROW_NUMBER.
reference_sql:
WITH ProductRevenue AS (
    SELECT
        p.ProductID,
        p.ProductName,
        p.CategoryID,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Products p
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
    GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName, p.CategoryID
),
RankedProducts AS (
    SELECT
        c.CategoryName,
        pr.ProductName,
        pr.TotalRevenue,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY pr.CategoryID ORDER BY pr.TotalRevenue DESC) AS RevenueRank
    FROM ProductRevenue pr
    JOIN Categories c ON pr.CategoryID = c.CategoryID
)
SELECT
    CategoryName,
    ProductName,
    TotalRevenue,
    RevenueRank
FROM RankedProducts
WHERE RevenueRank <= 2
ORDER BY CategoryName, RevenueRank;

question: For each product category, identify the top 2 products by total revenue (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)). If two products have the same total revenue within a category, they should share the same rank. Return the category name, product name, total revenue rounded to 2 decimal places, and the rank within the category. Only include rows where the rank is 1 or 2.
business_context: The VP of Merchandising wants to know which products are driving the most revenue in each category to guide upcoming promotional spend and inventory prioritization. She needs the top 2 revenue-generating products per category, accounting for discounts applied at the order level.
reference_sql:
WITH product_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        p.ProductID,
        p.ProductName,
        c.CategoryName,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Products p
    JOIN Categories c ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
    GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName, c.CategoryName
),
ranked_products AS (
    SELECT
        CategoryName,
        ProductName,
        TotalRevenue,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY CategoryName ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC) AS RevenueRank
    FROM product_revenue

SELECT

    ProductName,
    TotalRevenue,

FROM ranked_products

question: For each order placed by customer 'ALFKI', show the OrderID, OrderDate, and the date of their previous order (if any). Label the previous order date as PreviousOrderDate.
business_context: The Customer Success Manager wants to understand the purchasing cadence of key accounts. They've asked for a simple report showing each order alongside the prior order date for customer ALFKI, so they can spot gaps in purchasing activity.
reference_sql: SELECT OrderID, OrderDate, LAG(OrderDate) OVER (ORDER BY OrderDate) AS PreviousOrderDate FROM Orders WHERE CustomerID = 'ALFKI' ORDER BY OrderDate;

question: For each order placed by customer 'ALFKI', show the OrderID, OrderDate, and the date of their previous order (if any). Label the previous order date as PreviousOrderDate.
business_context: The Account Management team wants to understand the purchasing cadence of key accounts. They have asked for a simple view showing each order for customer ALFKI alongside the date of their prior order, so they can spot gaps in repeat purchasing.
reference_sql: SELECT OrderID, OrderDate, LAG(OrderDate) OVER (ORDER BY OrderDate) AS PreviousOrderDate FROM Orders WHERE CustomerID = 'ALFKI' ORDER BY OrderDate;

question: For each customer, calculate the revenue generated from their most recent order and the order immediately before it, then compute the month-over-month revenue change between those two consecutive orders. Return the customer ID, company name, the two most recent order dates, their respective revenues, and the revenue difference (most recent minus previous).
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify customers whose spending is trending downward. She needs to see, for each customer, how their last order compares to their second-to-last order in terms of revenue, so the team can prioritize outreach to customers showing a decline.
reference_sql:
WITH order_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        o.CustomerID,
        o.OrderID,
        o.OrderDate,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS Revenue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    GROUP BY o.CustomerID, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate
),
ranked_orders AS (
    SELECT
        CustomerID,
        OrderID,
        OrderDate,
        Revenue,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY OrderDate DESC) AS rn,
        LAG(Revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY OrderDate ASC) AS PrevRevenue,
        LAG(OrderDate) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY OrderDate ASC) AS PrevOrderDate
    FROM order_revenue
)
SELECT
    r.CustomerID,
    c.CompanyName,
    r.PrevOrderDate AS PreviousOrderDate,
    r.OrderDate AS MostRecentOrderDate,
    r.PrevRevenue AS PreviousOrderRevenue,
    r.Revenue AS MostRecentOrderRevenue,
    ROUND(r.Revenue - r.PrevRevenue, 2) AS RevenueChange
FROM ranked_orders r
JOIN Customers c ON r.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
WHERE r.rn = 1
  AND r.PrevRevenue IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY RevenueChange ASC

question: For each customer, list their orders in chronological order along with the previous order's date and the number of days between consecutive orders. Only include customers who have placed more than one order. Display the CustomerID, OrderID, OrderDate, the previous OrderDate (aliased as PrevOrderDate), and the gap in days (aliased as DaysSincePrevOrder).
business_context: The Head of Customer Success wants to understand purchasing cadence for repeat buyers. By identifying the gap between consecutive orders, the team can proactively reach out to customers who are overdue for a reorder and reduce churn risk.
reference_sql:
WITH OrderedOrders AS (
    SELECT
        CustomerID,
        OrderID,
        OrderDate,
        LAG(OrderDate) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY OrderDate) AS PrevOrderDate
    FROM Orders
),
CustomersWithMultipleOrders AS (
    SELECT CustomerID
    FROM Orders
    GROUP BY CustomerID
    HAVING COUNT(OrderID) > 1
)
SELECT
    oo.CustomerID,
    oo.OrderID,
    oo.OrderDate,
    oo.PrevOrderDate,
    CAST(julianday(oo.OrderDate) - julianday(oo.PrevOrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS DaysSincePrevOrder
FROM OrderedOrders oo
INNER JOIN CustomersWithMultipleOrders cm ON oo.CustomerID = cm.CustomerID
WHERE oo.PrevOrderDate IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY oo.CustomerID, oo.OrderDate

question: For each customer, calculate the month-over-month change in their total order revenue (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)) using LAG. Return the customer ID, company name, order month (formatted as YYYY-MM), current month revenue, previous month revenue, and the revenue change. Only include rows where a previous month exists. Order results by company name and order month.
business_context: The VP of Sales wants to identify customers whose monthly spending is declining so the account management team can proactively reach out before churn occurs. She needs a report showing each customer's revenue trend month by month, highlighting the delta from the prior month to spot patterns early.
reference_sql:
WITH monthly_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        o.CustomerID,
        c.CompanyName,
        STRFTIME('%Y-%m', o.OrderDate) AS order_month,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS monthly_total
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
    GROUP BY o.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, STRFTIME('%Y-%m', o.OrderDate)
),
lagged AS (
    SELECT
        CustomerID,
        CompanyName,
        order_month,
        monthly_total AS current_month_revenue,
        LAG(monthly_total) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY order_month) AS previous_month_revenue
    FROM monthly_revenue
)
SELECT
    CustomerID,
    CompanyName,
    order_month,
    current_month_revenue,
    previous_month_revenue,
    ROUND(current_month_revenue - previous_month_revenue, 2) AS revenue_change
FROM lagged
WHERE previous_month_revenue IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY CompanyName, order_month;

question: For each customer, calculate their order-over-order revenue change. Specifically, for every order placed by a customer, compute the total revenue of that order (sum of UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)), the total revenue of their previous order (using LAG), and the percentage change between the two. Return only rows where a previous order exists, and include the customer's company name, the current order ID and date, the current order revenue, the previous order revenue, and the percentage change rounded to 2 decimal places. Order results by CustomerID and OrderDate.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify customers whose spending is trending downward on a consecutive-order basis. She needs a report showing order-over-order revenue momentum for each customer so the account management team can prioritize outreach to customers showing significant revenue declines.
reference_sql: WITH OrderRevenue AS ( SELECT o.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS OrderRevenue FROM Orders o JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID GROUP BY o.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate ), OrderWithLag AS ( SELECT CustomerID, CompanyName, OrderID, OrderDate, OrderRevenue, LAG(OrderRevenue) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY OrderDate) AS PrevOrderRevenue FROM OrderRevenue ) SELECT CustomerID, CompanyName, OrderID, OrderDate, ROUND(OrderRevenue, 2) AS CurrentOrderRevenue, ROUND(PrevOrderRevenue, 2) AS PreviousOrderRevenue, ROUND((OrderRevenue - PrevOrderRevenue) / PrevOrderRevenue * 100, 2) AS PctChange FROM OrderWithLag WHERE PrevOrderRevenue IS NOT NULL ORDER BY CustomerID, OrderDate

question: Write a query that lists each order date and the cumulative total freight cost up to and including that date. Show the OrderID, OrderDate, Freight, and the running total of Freight ordered by OrderDate and OrderID.
business_context: The Head of Logistics at Northwind Traders wants to monitor how shipping costs accumulate over time. She needs a simple running total of freight charges ordered chronologically so she can identify periods of rapid cost growth.
reference_sql: SELECT OrderID, OrderDate, Freight, SUM(Freight) OVER (ORDER BY OrderDate, OrderID) AS RunningTotalFreight FROM Orders ORDER BY OrderDate, OrderID;

question: Write a query that shows each order date and the running total of freight costs over time. For each order, display the OrderID, OrderDate, Freight for that order, and the cumulative freight cost up to and including that order (ordered by OrderDate, then OrderID).
business_context: The Head of Logistics wants to monitor how shipping costs accumulate over time to better forecast freight budgets. They need a simple running total of freight charges ordered chronologically so they can spot periods of unusually high shipping spend.
reference_sql: SELECT OrderID, OrderDate, Freight, SUM(Freight) OVER (ORDER BY OrderDate, OrderID) AS RunningTotalFreight FROM Orders ORDER BY OrderDate, OrderID;

question: Write a query that calculates the monthly revenue for 2017 and a running total of revenue accumulated from the start of the year through each month. Monthly revenue should be calculated as the sum of (UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) from Order Details, joined to Orders filtered to the year 2017. Return the month number, monthly revenue (rounded to 2 decimal places), and the cumulative running total (rounded to 2 decimal places), ordered by month.
business_context: The Head of Finance at Northwind Traders wants to track how revenue builds throughout the fiscal year. She needs a month-by-month view of 2017 sales performance alongside a running cumulative total to compare against annual targets at any point in the year.
reference_sql:
WITH monthly_revenue AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(strftime('%m', o.OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS month_num,
    ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS monthly_revenue
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2017'
  GROUP BY strftime('%m', o.OrderDate)
)
SELECT
  month_num,
  monthly_revenue,
  ROUND(SUM(monthly_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month_num ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS running_total
FROM monthly_revenue
ORDER BY month_num;

question: Write a query that calculates the monthly revenue for 2017 and the running total of revenue accumulated from January through each month. Monthly revenue should be calculated as the sum of (UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) from Order Details, joined with Orders filtered to the year 2017. Show the month number, monthly revenue, and the cumulative running total ordered by month.
business_context: The VP of Sales wants to track how revenue builds up over the course of 2017 to assess whether the company is on pace to hit its annual targets. She needs a month-by-month view showing both the standalone monthly revenue and a cumulative year-to-date total so she can spot acceleration or slowdown trends.
reference_sql:
WITH monthly_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(strftime('%m', o.OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS order_month,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS monthly_revenue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2017'
    GROUP BY order_month
)
SELECT
    order_month,
    monthly_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(monthly_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS running_total
FROM monthly_revenue
ORDER BY order_month;

question: For each customer, calculate the cumulative (running) total revenue they have generated over time, ordered by order date. Revenue for each order should be calculated as the sum of (UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) across all order line items. Your result should include the customer's company name, each order date, the revenue for that specific order, and the running total revenue up to and including that order. Only include customers who have placed at least 5 orders, and limit the output to the top 10 customers by their final (maximum) cumulative revenue.
business_context: The Head of Sales at Northwind Traders wants to identify the company's most valuable long-term customers by tracking how their cumulative spend has grown over time. This analysis will help prioritize which accounts should receive dedicated account managers and premium service agreements. The VP of Revenue has asked for this report ahead of the upcoming quarterly business reviews.
reference_sql:
WITH order_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        o.CustomerID,
        o.OrderID,
        CAST(o.OrderDate AS DATE) AS OrderDate,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS OrderRevenue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    GROUP BY o.CustomerID, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate
),
customer_order_counts AS (
    SELECT CustomerID
    FROM Orders
    GROUP BY CustomerID
    HAVING COUNT(OrderID) >= 5
),
running_totals AS (
    SELECT
        orv.CustomerID,
        c.CompanyName,
        orv.OrderDate,
        orv.OrderRevenue,
        SUM(orv.OrderRevenue) OVER (
            PARTITION BY orv.CustomerID
            ORDER BY orv.OrderDate, orv.OrderID
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS RunningTotalRevenue
    FROM order_revenue orv
    JOIN Customers c ON orv.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
    WHERE orv.CustomerID IN (SELECT CustomerID FROM customer_order_counts)
),
max_running AS (
    SELECT
        CustomerID,
        MAX(RunningTotalRevenue) AS FinalCumulativeRevenue
    FROM running_totals
    GROUP BY CustomerID
),
top_customers AS (
    SELECT CustomerID
    FROM max_running
    ORDER BY FinalCumulativeRevenue DESC
    LIMIT 10
)
SELECT
    rt.CompanyName,
    rt.OrderDate,
    ROUND(rt.OrderRevenue, 2) AS OrderRevenue,
    ROUND(rt.RunningTotalRevenue, 2) AS RunningTotalRevenue
FROM running_totals rt
WHERE rt.CustomerID IN (SELECT CustomerID FROM top_customers)
ORDER BY rt.CompanyName, rt.OrderDate, rt.RunningTotalRevenue

question: List each product name along with its category name. Return the product name and category name for all products.
business_context: The Merchandising Manager wants a simple reference list of all products and their corresponding categories to use in a quarterly product catalog update. She needs both the product name and the category it belongs to in a single report.
reference_sql: SELECT p.ProductName, c.CategoryName FROM Products p JOIN Categories c ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID

question: List each product name along with its category name. Return the product name and category name for all products.
business_context: The merchandising team wants a simple reference sheet that maps every product to its category for an upcoming catalog update. The Head of Merchandising has asked for a clean list showing product names alongside their corresponding category names.
reference_sql: SELECT p.ProductName, c.CategoryName FROM Products p JOIN Categories c ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID;

question: For each product category, calculate the total revenue generated (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)), the number of distinct orders, and the number of distinct products sold. Return the results ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Merchandising wants to understand which product categories are driving the most revenue and order volume. This analysis will inform decisions about inventory investment and promotional priorities for the upcoming quarter.
reference_sql: SELECT c.CategoryName, ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS TotalRevenue, COUNT(DISTINCT od.OrderID) AS DistinctOrders, COUNT(DISTINCT od.ProductID) AS DistinctProducts FROM Categories c JOIN Products p ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID JOIN "Order Details" od ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC

question: Write a query that returns each product's name, its category name, its supplier's company name, and the total quantity ordered across all orders. Only include products that have been ordered at least once. Sort the results by total quantity ordered in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Procurement wants a consolidated view of product demand alongside supplier and category information to identify which suppliers and categories are driving the highest order volumes. This will help prioritize supplier negotiations and inventory restocking decisions.
reference_sql: SELECT p.ProductName, c.CategoryName, s.CompanyName AS SupplierName, SUM(od.Quantity) AS TotalQuantityOrdered FROM Products p JOIN Categories c ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID JOIN Suppliers s ON p.SupplierID = s.SupplierID JOIN "Order Details" od ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName, c.CategoryName, s.CompanyName ORDER BY TotalQuantityOrdered DESC

question: For each product category, identify the top-performing sales representative (by total revenue generated) along with the total revenue, total units sold, and number of distinct customers they served within that category. Only include results where the sales rep has handled at least 5 distinct orders in that category. Display the category name, employee full name, total revenue (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)), total units sold, distinct customer count, and distinct order count, ordered by category name and total revenue descending.
business_context: The VP of Sales wants to identify category champions — the single best-performing sales rep for each product category — to build a specialized incentive program and assign mentorship roles. She needs to see not just revenue but also breadth of customer reach to ensure the reps are truly driving category growth across the customer base.
reference_sql:
WITH CategoryRepRevenue AS (
    SELECT
        c.CategoryName,
        e.EmployeeID,
        e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS EmployeeFullName,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS TotalRevenue,
        SUM(od.Quantity) AS TotalUnitsSold,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.CustomerID) AS DistinctCustomers,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.OrderID) AS DistinctOrders
    FROM "Order Details" od
    JOIN Orders o ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
    JOIN Products p ON od.ProductID = p.ProductID
    JOIN Categories c ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID
    JOIN Employees e ON o.EmployeeID = e.EmployeeID
    GROUP BY c.CategoryName, e.EmployeeID, EmployeeFullName
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.OrderID) >= 5
),
RankedReps AS (
    SELECT
        CategoryName,
        EmployeeFullName,
        TotalRevenue,
        TotalUnitsSold,
        DistinctCustomers,
        DistinctOrders,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY CategoryName ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC) AS RevenueRank
    FROM CategoryRepRevenue
)
SELECT
    CategoryName,
    EmployeeFullName,
    TotalRevenue,
    TotalUnitsSold,
    DistinctCustomers,
    DistinctOrders
FROM RankedReps
WHERE RevenueRank = 1
ORDER BY CategoryName ASC, TotalRevenue DESC

question: For each product category, identify the top-performing employee (by total revenue generated) along with the supplier who provides the most products in that category. Return the category name, the employee's full name, their total revenue for that category (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)), the supplier's company name, and the count of products that supplier has in the category. Only include categories where at least 5 distinct orders have been placed.
business_context: The VP of Sales wants a cross-functional performance report to plan Q1 incentives and supplier negotiations. Specifically, they need to know which employee is driving the most revenue per category, and which supplier dominates each category's product catalog, so that top performers can be rewarded and key supplier relationships can be prioritized.
reference_sql: WITH category_employee_revenue AS ( SELECT c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName, e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS EmployeeFullName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS TotalRevenue, COUNT(DISTINCT o.OrderID) AS OrderCount FROM Categories c JOIN Products p ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID JOIN "Order Details" od ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN Orders o ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID JOIN Employees e ON o.EmployeeID = e.EmployeeID GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName, e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName ), top_employee_per_category AS ( SELECT CategoryID, CategoryName, EmployeeID, EmployeeFullName, TotalRevenue, OrderCount, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY CategoryID ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC) AS RevenueRank FROM category_employee_revenue WHERE OrderCount >= 5 ), category_supplier_counts AS ( SELECT c.CategoryID, s.SupplierID, s.CompanyName AS SupplierName, COUNT(p.ProductID) AS ProductCount, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.CategoryID ORDER BY COUNT(p.ProductID) DESC) AS SupplierRank FROM Categories c JOIN Products p ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID JOIN Suppliers s ON p.SupplierID = s.SupplierID GROUP BY c.CategoryID, s.SupplierID, s.CompanyName ) SELECT t.CategoryName, t.EmployeeFullName, ROUND(t.TotalRevenue, 2) AS TotalRevenue, s.SupplierName, s.ProductCount FROM top_employee_per_category t JOIN category_supplier_counts s ON t.CategoryID = s.CategoryID WHERE t.RevenueRank = 1 AND s.SupplierRank = 1 ORDER BY t.TotalRevenue DESC

question: Write a query that retrieves each product's name and unit price, along with the average unit price of all products in the same category. Use a correlated subquery to calculate the category average.
business_context: The Head of Merchandising wants to quickly identify how each product's price compares to its category peers. They need a simple report showing each product's name, its price, and the average price of products in the same category to spot potential pricing outliers.
reference_sql: SELECT ProductName, UnitPrice, (SELECT AVG(p2.UnitPrice) FROM Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p1.CategoryID) AS CategoryAvgPrice FROM Products p1 ORDER BY p1.CategoryID, p1.ProductName;

question: Write a query that returns each product's name, unit price, and the average unit price of all products in the same category. Use a correlated subquery to calculate the category average.
business_context: The Category Manager wants to quickly identify which products are priced above or below the average for their category. This will help inform upcoming pricing review meetings and potential promotional bundling decisions.
reference_sql: SELECT p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice, (SELECT AVG(p2.UnitPrice) FROM Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID) AS AvgCategoryPrice FROM Products p ORDER BY p.CategoryID, p.ProductName

question: For each customer, find their most recent order date and the total number of orders they have placed. Return the CustomerID, CompanyName, most recent order date, and total order count. Use a correlated subquery to determine the most recent order date for each customer.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify which customers have been recently active versus those who may be at risk of churning. By seeing each customer's latest order date alongside their total order history, the sales team can prioritize outreach efforts and tailor retention strategies accordingly.
reference_sql: SELECT c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, (SELECT MAX(o.OrderDate) FROM Orders o WHERE o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID) AS MostRecentOrderDate, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders o WHERE o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID) AS TotalOrders FROM Customers c ORDER BY MostRecentOrderDate DESC

question: For each customer, find their most recent order date and the total number of orders they have placed. Return the customer's CompanyName, their most recent OrderDate, and their total order count. Use a correlated subquery to determine the most recent order date for each customer.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify which customers have been active recently versus those who may be lapsing. They need a report showing each customer's latest order date and overall order volume to help prioritize outreach efforts for the upcoming quarter.
reference_sql: SELECT c.CompanyName, (SELECT MAX(o.OrderDate) FROM Orders o WHERE o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID) AS MostRecentOrderDate, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders o WHERE o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID) AS TotalOrders FROM Customers c ORDER BY MostRecentOrderDate DESC

question: For each customer, find the single most recent order where the order's freight cost exceeded the average freight cost of all that customer's orders. Return the customer's company name, the order ID, the order date, the freight amount for that order, and the customer's overall average freight cost rounded to 2 decimal places. Only include customers who have placed at least 5 orders. Order results by the freight amount of the qualifying order descending.
business_context: The Head of Logistics has noticed that certain high-value shipments are disproportionately inflating shipping costs for specific accounts. She wants to identify, for each customer with a meaningful order history, the most recent 'outlier' order where freight exceeded their own average — so the team can renegotiate shipping contracts or offer freight discounts proactively.
reference_sql: WITH customer_freight_stats AS ( SELECT CustomerID, AVG(Freight) AS avg_freight, COUNT(OrderID) AS order_count FROM Orders GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(OrderID) >= 5 ), qualifying_orders AS ( SELECT o.CustomerID, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.Freight FROM Orders o JOIN customer_freight_stats cfs ON o.CustomerID = cfs.CustomerID WHERE o.Freight > cfs.avg_freight AND o.OrderDate = ( SELECT MAX(o2.OrderDate) FROM Orders o2 JOIN customer_freight_stats cfs2 ON o2.CustomerID = cfs2.CustomerID WHERE o2.CustomerID = o.CustomerID AND o2.Freight > cfs2.avg_freight ) ) SELECT c.CompanyName, qo.OrderID, qo.OrderDate, qo.Freight, ROUND(cfs.avg_freight, 2) AS avg_freight FROM qualifying_orders qo JOIN Customers c ON qo.CustomerID = c.CustomerID JOIN customer_freight_stats cfs ON qo.CustomerID = cfs.CustomerID ORDER BY qo.Freight DESC

question: For each customer, find the single most expensive order they have ever placed (by total order value after discounts), and return the customer's company name, the order ID, the order date, and the total order value. If a customer has multiple orders tied for the highest value, return all of them. Only include customers who have placed at least 3 orders.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify each customer's 'peak' order to understand purchasing behavior at its highest point. This analysis will help the account management team prioritize outreach and design loyalty incentives for high-value customers.
reference_sql:
WITH OrderTotals AS (
    SELECT
        o.OrderID,
        o.CustomerID,
        o.OrderDate,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS OrderValue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.CustomerID, o.OrderDate
),
CustomerOrderCounts AS (
    SELECT CustomerID
    FROM Orders
    GROUP BY CustomerID
    HAVING COUNT(OrderID) >= 3
)
SELECT
    c.CompanyName,
    ot.OrderID,
    ot.OrderDate,
    ROUND(ot.OrderValue, 2) AS TotalOrderValue
FROM OrderTotals ot
JOIN Customers c ON ot.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
JOIN CustomerOrderCounts coc ON ot.CustomerID = coc.CustomerID
WHERE ot.OrderValue = (
    SELECT MAX(ot2.OrderValue)
    FROM OrderTotals ot2
    WHERE ot2.CustomerID = ot.CustomerID
)
ORDER BY TotalOrderValue DESC, c.CompanyName;

question: Find the total number of invoices and the overall revenue generated, grouped by billing country. Return the billing country, invoice count, and total revenue, ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants a high-level summary of sales performance across different countries. This will help identify the top markets contributing the most to overall store revenue and guide regional marketing spend decisions.
reference_sql: SELECT BillingCountry, COUNT(InvoiceId) AS InvoiceCount, SUM(Total) AS TotalRevenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC

question: Find the total number of invoices and the overall revenue generated, grouped by billing country. Return the billing country, invoice count, and total revenue, ordered by total revenue from highest to lowest.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants a quick snapshot of how different countries are performing in terms of sales volume and revenue. This will help prioritize which markets to invest in for upcoming promotional campaigns.
reference_sql: SELECT BillingCountry, COUNT(InvoiceId) AS InvoiceCount, SUM(Total) AS TotalRevenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC

question: For each billing country, calculate the total revenue, number of invoices, and average invoice value. Only include countries that have generated more than $40 in total revenue. Return the results sorted by total revenue in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants to identify high-value markets for a targeted promotional campaign. She needs a country-level breakdown of invoice activity to prioritize regions where marketing spend would have the greatest impact.
reference_sql: SELECT BillingCountry, SUM(Total) AS TotalRevenue, COUNT(InvoiceId) AS NumberOfInvoices, ROUND(AVG(Total), 2) AS AvgInvoiceValue FROM Invoice GROUP BY BillingCountry HAVING SUM(Total) > 40 ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC

question: For each billing country, calculate the total revenue, number of invoices, and average invoice value. Only include countries that have generated more than $40 in total revenue. Return the results ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants to identify high-value markets for a targeted marketing campaign. She needs a country-level summary of invoice activity to determine where Chinook's strongest revenue bases are located, focusing only on markets with meaningful spend.
reference_sql: SELECT BillingCountry, SUM(Total) AS TotalRevenue, COUNT(InvoiceId) AS NumberOfInvoices, ROUND(AVG(Total), 2) AS AvgInvoiceValue FROM Invoice GROUP BY BillingCountry HAVING SUM(Total) > 40 ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC

question: Using only the Invoice table, calculate for each billing country: the total number of invoices, the total revenue, the average invoice value, the minimum and maximum invoice values, and a revenue percentile rank (as a percentage, rounded to 2 decimal places) of each country relative to all other countries based on total revenue. Return only countries with more than 5 invoices, ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The VP of International Sales wants a self-contained revenue breakdown by country to identify top-performing markets and understand the spread of invoice values without joining to customer records. She specifically wants to know each country's revenue standing relative to all other countries as a percentile, so she can prioritize regional marketing budgets for next quarter.
reference_sql: WITH country_stats AS ( SELECT BillingCountry, COUNT(InvoiceId) AS total_invoices, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS total_revenue, ROUND(AVG(Total), 2) AS avg_invoice_value, ROUND(MIN(Total), 2) AS min_invoice_value, ROUND(MAX(Total), 2) AS max_invoice_value FROM Invoice GROUP BY BillingCountry HAVING COUNT(InvoiceId) > 5 ) SELECT BillingCountry, total_invoices, total_revenue, avg_invoice_value, min_invoice_value, max_invoice_value, ROUND( 100.0 * PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_revenue), 2 ) AS revenue_percentile_rank FROM country_stats ORDER BY total_revenue DESC

question: For each billing country, calculate the total revenue, number of invoices, average invoice value, and the percentage contribution of that country's revenue to the overall global revenue. Only include countries where the total revenue exceeds the global average revenue per country. Return results ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The VP of International Sales wants a high-level revenue breakdown by country to identify top-performing markets. She specifically wants to focus on countries that are performing above average so the team can double down on successful regions and inform budget allocation for the next fiscal year.
reference_sql:
WITH country_stats AS (
    SELECT
        BillingCountry,
        SUM(Total) AS total_revenue,
        COUNT(InvoiceId) AS invoice_count,
        AVG(Total) AS avg_invoice_value
    FROM Invoice
    GROUP BY BillingCountry
),
global_stats AS (
    SELECT
        SUM(Total) AS global_revenue,
        SUM(Total) / COUNT(DISTINCT BillingCountry) AS avg_revenue_per_country
    FROM Invoice
)
SELECT
    cs.BillingCountry,
    cs.total_revenue,
    cs.invoice_count,
    ROUND(cs.avg_invoice_value, 2) AS avg_invoice_value,
    ROUND((cs.total_revenue / gs.global_revenue) * 100, 2) AS pct_of_global_revenue
FROM country_stats cs
CROSS JOIN global_stats gs
WHERE cs.total_revenue > gs.avg_revenue_per_country
ORDER BY cs.total_revenue DESC

question: Find all countries that have more than 5 customers. Return the country name and the number of customers, ordered by customer count in descending order.
business_context: The Head of International Sales wants to identify markets with a significant customer base to prioritize regional marketing campaigns. They need a list of countries where Chinook has more than 5 registered customers.
reference_sql: SELECT Country, COUNT(CustomerId) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer GROUP BY Country HAVING COUNT(CustomerId) > 5 ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC

question: Find all countries that have more than 5 customers. Return the country name and the number of customers, ordered by customer count in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Marketing wants to identify high-potential markets for a targeted promotional campaign. She needs a list of countries where Chinook already has a solid customer base (more than 5 customers) to prioritize marketing spend effectively.
reference_sql: SELECT Country, COUNT(CustomerId) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer GROUP BY Country HAVING COUNT(CustomerId) > 5 ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC

question: Identify all artists who have released more than 3 albums in the Chinook store. For each qualifying artist, return their name and the total number of albums they have available. Order the results by album count in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Content Partnerships wants to identify prolific artists in our catalog to prioritize licensing renegotiations. Specifically, they need a list of artists with a strong album presence (more than 3 albums) to focus outreach efforts and ensure contract terms are competitive.
reference_sql: SELECT ar.Name AS ArtistName, COUNT(al.AlbumId) AS AlbumCount FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(al.AlbumId) > 3 ORDER BY AlbumCount DESC

question: Identify all customers who have made more than 5 purchases (invoices) and whose total spending across all invoices exceeds $40. Return the customer's full name, total number of invoices, and their cumulative spend, ordered by cumulative spend descending.
business_context: The Head of Customer Success wants to identify high-engagement buyers for a new VIP loyalty program. Specifically, they need customers who are both frequent purchasers (more than 5 invoices) and high spenders (over $40 total) to target with exclusive offers.
reference_sql: SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(i.InvoiceId) AS TotalInvoices, SUM(i.Total) AS TotalSpend FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName HAVING COUNT(i.InvoiceId) > 5 AND SUM(i.Total) > 40 ORDER BY TotalSpend DESC

question: Identify artists whose tracks have been purchased across at least 5 distinct countries, and whose total revenue from track sales exceeds $100. For each qualifying artist, return their name, the number of distinct countries they've sold to, the total number of tracks sold, and their total revenue. Order the results by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Global Licensing asks: 'We want to identify artists with strong international appeal and meaningful revenue contribution — specifically those who have sold tracks in at least 5 different countries and generated over $100 in total sales. This will help us prioritize licensing negotiations and promotional partnerships.'
reference_sql:
WITH artist_sales AS (
    SELECT
        ar.ArtistId,
        ar.Name AS ArtistName,
        i.BillingCountry,
        il.Quantity,
        il.UnitPrice
    FROM Artist ar
    JOIN Album al ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId
    JOIN Track t ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
    JOIN InvoiceLine il ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
    JOIN Invoice i ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
)
SELECT
    ArtistName,
    COUNT(DISTINCT BillingCountry) AS distinct_countries,
    SUM(Quantity) AS total_tracks_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(Quantity * UnitPrice), 2) AS total_revenue
FROM artist_sales
GROUP BY ArtistId, ArtistName
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT BillingCountry) >= 5
   AND SUM(Quantity * UnitPrice) > 100
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

question: Identify artists whose tracks have been purchased in at least 5 distinct countries, and for whom the average revenue per invoice line (UnitPrice × Quantity) across all their tracks exceeds $1.00. Return the artist name, number of distinct countries, total revenue generated, and average revenue per invoice line, ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Global Sales wants to identify internationally successful artists who also generate strong per-transaction revenue, to prioritize them for featured placement and promotional campaigns across regional storefronts. She needs both breadth (global reach) and depth (revenue quality) filters applied simultaneously.
reference_sql:
WITH artist_sales AS (
    SELECT
        ar.ArtistId,
        ar.Name AS ArtistName,
        COUNT(DISTINCT i.BillingCountry) AS DistinctCountries,
        SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS TotalRevenue,
        AVG(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS AvgRevenuePerLine
    FROM Artist ar
    JOIN Album al ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId
    JOIN Track t ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
    JOIN InvoiceLine il ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
    JOIN Invoice i ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
    GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT i.BillingCountry) >= 5
       AND AVG(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) > 1.00
)
SELECT
    ArtistName,
    DistinctCountries,
    TotalRevenue,
    AvgRevenuePerLine
FROM artist_sales
ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC;

question: Using a CTE, calculate the total revenue generated by each billing country. Return the country name and its total revenue, ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of International Sales wants a quick summary of revenue contribution by country to identify which markets are performing best. This will inform upcoming regional marketing budget decisions.
reference_sql: WITH CountryRevenue AS ( SELECT BillingCountry, SUM(Total) AS TotalRevenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY BillingCountry ) SELECT BillingCountry, TotalRevenue FROM CountryRevenue ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC

question: Using a CTE, find the total number of invoices and the total revenue generated per country. Return the billing country, invoice count, and total revenue, ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants a high-level summary of sales performance by country to identify the top markets for Chinook Digital Store. She needs this broken out by invoice count and total revenue to prioritize regional marketing campaigns.
reference_sql:
WITH country_sales AS (
    SELECT
        BillingCountry,
        COUNT(InvoiceId) AS invoice_count,
        SUM(Total) AS total_revenue
    FROM Invoice
    GROUP BY BillingCountry
)
SELECT
    BillingCountry,
    invoice_count,
    total_revenue

question: Using a CTE, identify the top 5 genres by total revenue generated from track sales. For each genre, return the genre name, total number of tracks sold, and total revenue. Order the results by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Catalog Strategy wants to understand which music genres are driving the most revenue on the platform. This will inform decisions about which genres to prioritize for new content acquisitions and promotional campaigns.
reference_sql:
WITH GenreRevenue AS (
    SELECT
        g.Name AS GenreName,
        SUM(il.Quantity) AS TotalTracksSold,
        SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM InvoiceLine il
    JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
    JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
    GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
)
SELECT
    GenreName,
    TotalTracksSold,
    TotalRevenue
FROM GenreRevenue
ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC
LIMIT 5;

question: Using a CTE, identify the top 5 customers by total amount spent, and for each of these customers, show their full name, country, total amount spent, and the name of their assigned support representative.
business_context: The Head of Customer Success wants to identify the highest-value customers globally to prioritize for a VIP loyalty program. She needs to know which sales support agents are already managing these top customers so she can coordinate outreach effectively.
reference_sql:
WITH CustomerSpend AS (
    SELECT
        c.CustomerId,
        c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS CustomerName,
        c.Country,
        c.SupportRepId,
        SUM(i.Total) AS TotalSpent
    FROM Customer c
    JOIN Invoice i ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
    GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName, c.Country, c.SupportRepId
)
SELECT
    cs.CustomerName,
    cs.Country,
    cs.TotalSpent,
    e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS SupportRepName
FROM CustomerSpend cs
JOIN Employee e ON cs.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId
ORDER BY cs.TotalSpent DESC
LIMIT 5;

question: For each sales support agent, identify their top-performing customer (by total revenue generated) and calculate how that customer's spend compares to the agent's overall average customer spend. Return the agent's full name, the top customer's full name, the top customer's total spend, the agent's average customer spend, and the difference between the two. Order results by the agent's average customer spend descending.
business_context: The VP of Sales wants to evaluate how each support agent's best customer stacks up against their typical customer. This will help identify agents who rely heavily on a single whale customer versus those with a more balanced and healthy book of business.
reference_sql:
WITH customer_spend AS (
    SELECT
        c.CustomerId,
        c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS CustomerName,
        c.SupportRepId,
        SUM(i.Total) AS TotalSpend
    FROM Customer c
    JOIN Invoice i ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
    GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName, c.SupportRepId
),
agent_stats AS (
    SELECT
        SupportRepId,
        AVG(TotalSpend) AS AvgCustomerSpend
    FROM customer_spend
    GROUP BY SupportRepId
),
ranked_customers AS (
    SELECT
        cs.CustomerId,
        cs.CustomerName,
        cs.SupportRepId,
        cs.TotalSpend,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY cs.SupportRepId ORDER BY cs.TotalSpend DESC) AS SpendRank
    FROM customer_spend cs
)
SELECT
    e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS AgentName,
    rc.CustomerName AS TopCustomerName,
    ROUND(rc.TotalSpend, 2) AS TopCustomerSpend,
    ROUND(ag.AvgCustomerSpend, 2) AS AgentAvgCustomerSpend,
    ROUND(rc.TotalSpend - ag.AvgCustomerSpend, 2) AS SpendDifference
FROM ranked_customers rc
JOIN agent_stats ag ON rc.SupportRepId = ag.SupportRepId
JOIN Employee e ON rc.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId
WHERE rc.SpendRank = 1
ORDER BY ag.AvgCustomerSpend DESC

question: For each sales support agent, calculate their total revenue generated, the number of unique customers they support, and their percentage contribution to overall store revenue. Rank agents from highest to lowest revenue contribution. Return the agent's full name, total revenue, customer count, revenue percentage (rounded to 2 decimal places), and their rank.
business_context: The VP of Sales wants a comprehensive performance dashboard for all sales support agents ahead of the annual review cycle. She needs to understand each agent's revenue impact relative to the total store revenue to make informed decisions about bonuses and team restructuring.
reference_sql: WITH agent_revenue AS ( SELECT e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS AgentName, COUNT(DISTINCT c.CustomerId) AS CustomerCount, SUM(i.Total) AS TotalRevenue FROM Employee e JOIN Customer c ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId JOIN Invoice i ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName ), store_total AS ( SELECT SUM(Total) AS GrandTotal FROM Invoice ) SELECT ar.AgentName, ar.TotalRevenue, ar.CustomerCount, ROUND(ar.TotalRevenue * 100.0 / st.GrandTotal, 2) AS RevenuePercentage, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ar.TotalRevenue DESC) AS RevenueRank FROM agent_revenue ar CROSS JOIN store_total st ORDER BY RevenueRank

question: For each billing country, rank the invoices by their total amount in descending order using RANK(). Return the billing country, invoice ID, total amount, and the rank of each invoice within its country.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants to identify the highest-value transactions in each country to understand spending patterns across our global customer base. This will help prioritize regional marketing campaigns and loyalty rewards for top spenders.
reference_sql: SELECT BillingCountry, InvoiceId, Total, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY BillingCountry ORDER BY Total DESC) AS RevenueRank FROM Invoice

question: Rank all customers by their total spending (sum of all invoice totals) in descending order. Return the customer's full name, total amount spent, and their rank. Use RANK() so that ties share the same rank.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants to identify the top spenders across the platform to target them with a VIP loyalty program. They need a ranked list of all customers by lifetime spend so the marketing team can prioritize outreach.
reference_sql: SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName, SUM(i.Total) AS TotalSpent, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(i.Total) DESC) AS SpendRank FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY SpendRank

question: For each billing country, identify the top 2 customers by total amount spent. Return the country, customer full name, their total spend, and their rank within the country. If two customers have the same total spend, they should share the same rank.
business_context: The Head of Regional Sales wants to identify the highest-value customers in each country for a targeted VIP loyalty program. She needs to know the top 2 spenders per country, with ties handled fairly, to ensure no high-value customer is accidentally excluded from the program.
reference_sql:
WITH CustomerSpend AS (
    SELECT
        c.CustomerId,
        c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS CustomerName,
        i.BillingCountry AS Country,
        SUM(i.Total) AS TotalSpend
    FROM Customer c
    JOIN Invoice i ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
    GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName, i.BillingCountry
),
RankedCustomers AS (
    SELECT
        Country,
        CustomerName,
        TotalSpend,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY Country ORDER BY TotalSpend DESC) AS SpendRank
    FROM CustomerSpend
)
SELECT
    Country,
    CustomerName,
    TotalSpend,
    SpendRank
FROM RankedCustomers
WHERE SpendRank <= 2
ORDER BY Country, SpendRank;

question: For each billing country, rank customers by their total lifetime spend (sum of all invoice totals). Return the country, customer full name, total spend, and their rank within the country. Only include the top 3 ranked customers per country (ties should share the same rank using DENSE_RANK).
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants to identify the top-spending customers in each country to target them with a VIP loyalty program. She needs the top 3 spenders per country, accounting for tied spend amounts, so that no eligible customer is accidentally excluded.
reference_sql:
WITH CustomerSpend AS (
    SELECT
        c.CustomerId,
        c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS CustomerName,
        i.BillingCountry AS Country,
        SUM(i.Total) AS TotalSpend
    FROM Customer c

    GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName, i.BillingCountry
),
RankedCustomers AS (
    SELECT

question: For each country, identify the top 2 customers by total lifetime spend. Return the customer's full name, country, their total spend, and their rank within the country. In case of ties, customers with the same spend should share the same rank. Only include rows where the rank is 1 or 2.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants to launch a VIP loyalty program targeting the top 2 spenders in each country. reference_sql:
WITH CustomerSpend AS (

question: For each genre, identify the top 3 best-selling tracks by total revenue (UnitPrice × Quantity). In cases where tracks are tied in revenue within the same genre, assign the same rank but still return all tied tracks within the top 3 positions. Return the genre name, track name, total revenue for that track, and its rank within the genre. Order results by genre name and rank.
business_context: The Head of Content Strategy wants to understand which tracks drive the most revenue within each music genre. This analysis will inform editorial decisions about which genres and tracks to feature prominently in marketing campaigns and homepage placements. Ties in revenue should be preserved so no popular track is inadvertently excluded.
reference_sql:
WITH TrackRevenue AS (
    SELECT
        t.TrackId,
        t.Name AS TrackName,
        g.Name AS GenreName,
        SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Track t
    JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
    JOIN InvoiceLine il ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
    GROUP BY t.TrackId, t.Name, g.Name
),
RankedTracks AS (
    SELECT
        GenreName,
        TrackName,
        TotalRevenue,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY GenreName ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC) AS RevenueRank
    FROM TrackRevenue
)
SELECT
    GenreName,
    TrackName,
    TotalRevenue,
    RevenueRank
FROM RankedTracks
WHERE RevenueRank <= 3
ORDER BY GenreName, RevenueRank;

question: For each invoice, show the invoice ID, invoice date, total amount, and the total amount from the previous invoice (ordered by invoice date) for the same customer. Name the previous total column 'prev_invoice_total'.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants to quickly spot customers whose spending has changed between consecutive purchases. A simple side-by-side view of each invoice total alongside the prior invoice total will help the team flag notable drops or spikes in customer spend.
reference_sql: SELECT InvoiceId, CustomerId, InvoiceDate, Total, LAG(Total) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerId ORDER BY InvoiceDate) AS prev_invoice_total FROM Invoice ORDER BY CustomerId, InvoiceDate;

question: For each invoice, show the invoice ID, invoice date, total amount, and the total amount of the previous invoice (ordered by invoice date) for the same customer. Name the previous invoice total as 'prev_invoice_total'.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants to quickly spot customers whose spending is changing over time. As a first step, she asks for a simple side-by-side view of each invoice alongside the customer's immediately preceding purchase total so the finance team can eyeball increases or decreases at a glance.
reference_sql: SELECT InvoiceId, CustomerId, InvoiceDate, Total, LAG(Total) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerId ORDER BY InvoiceDate) AS prev_invoice_total FROM Invoice ORDER BY CustomerId, InvoiceDate;

question: For each customer, retrieve their invoices ordered by date and show the current invoice total alongside the previous invoice total (using LAG). Calculate the difference between the current and previous invoice totals. Return the customer's full name, invoice date, current total, previous total, and the difference. Only include rows where a previous invoice exists.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants to understand how customer spending changes between consecutive purchases. Identifying customers whose invoice amounts are growing or declining over time can help the sales support team prioritize outreach and upsell opportunities.
reference_sql:
WITH invoice_with_lag AS (
    SELECT
        c.CustomerId,
        c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS CustomerName,
        i.InvoiceDate,
        i.Total AS CurrentTotal,
        LAG(i.Total) OVER (PARTITION BY c.CustomerId ORDER BY i.InvoiceDate) AS PreviousTotal
    FROM Customer c
    JOIN Invoice i ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
)
SELECT
    CustomerName,
    InvoiceDate,
    CurrentTotal,
    PreviousTotal,
    CurrentTotal - PreviousTotal AS TotalDifference
FROM invoice_with_lag
WHERE PreviousTotal IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY CustomerName, InvoiceDate

question: For each customer, calculate their invoice totals in chronological order and show the difference between each invoice and their previous invoice.
