The Head of Global Demographics asks: 'Which countries are growing faster or slower than others at their population scale, and by how much?' This will inform targeted intervention strategies for under- and over-performing nations within each tier.
reference_sql:
SELECT
    f.name,
    CASE
        WHEN f.population < 10000000 THEN 'small'
        WHEN f.population <= 100000000 THEN 'medium'
        ELSE 'large'
    END AS population_tier,
    f.population_growth,
    ROUND((
        SELECT AVG(f2.population_growth)
        FROM facts f2
        WHERE f2.population IS NOT NULL
          AND f2.population_growth IS NOT NULL
          AND CASE
                WHEN f2.population < 10000000 THEN 'small'
                WHEN f2.population <= 100000000 THEN 'medium'
                ELSE 'large'
              END = CASE
                        WHEN f.population < 10000000 THEN 'small'
                        WHEN f.population <= 100000000 THEN 'medium'
                        ELSE 'large'
                    END
    ), 4) AS tier_avg_growth,
    CASE
        WHEN f.population_growth > (
            SELECT AVG(f2.population_growth)
            FROM facts f2
            WHERE f2.population IS NOT NULL
              AND f2.population_growth IS NOT NULL
              AND CASE
                    WHEN f2.population < 10000000 THEN 'small'
                    WHEN f2.population <= 100000000 THEN 'medium'
                    ELSE 'large'
                  END = CASE
                            WHEN f.population < 10000000 THEN 'small'
                            WHEN f.population <= 100000000 THEN 'medium'
                            ELSE 'large'
                        END
        ) THEN 'above'
        WHEN f.population_growth < (
            SELECT AVG(f2.population_growth)
            FROM facts f2
            WHERE f2.population IS NOT NULL
              AND f2.population_growth IS NOT NULL
              AND CASE
                    WHEN f2.population < 10000000 THEN 'small'
                    WHEN f2.population <= 100000000 THEN 'medium'
                    ELSE 'large'
                  END = CASE
                            WHEN f.population < 10000000 THEN 'small'
                            WHEN f.population <= 100000000 THEN 'medium'
                            ELSE 'large'
                        END
        ) THEN 'below'
        ELSE 'equal'
    END AS vs_tier_avg
FROM facts f
WHERE f.population IS NOT NULL
  AND f.population_growth IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY population_tier ASC, f.population_growth DESC

question: How many products does Northwind Traders currently offer in each category? Return the CategoryID and the total number of products for each category, ordered by the total number of products in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Merchandising wants a quick summary of how the product catalog is distributed across categories. This will help prioritize which categories to expand or consolidate in the upcoming product line review.
reference_sql: SELECT CategoryID, COUNT(ProductID) AS TotalProducts FROM Products GROUP BY CategoryID ORDER BY TotalProducts DESC;

question: How many customers does Northwind have in each country? Return the country and the total number of customers, ordered by customer count from highest to lowest.
business_context: The VP of Sales is planning a regional marketing campaign and wants to understand where Northwind's customer base is concentrated. She has asked for a breakdown of the number of customers by country to help prioritize outreach efforts.
reference_sql: SELECT Country, COUNT(CustomerID) AS CustomerCount FROM Customers GROUP BY Country ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC

question: How many products does Northwind Traders currently offer in each category? Return the CategoryID and the total number of products, ordered by the count of products in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Merchandising wants a quick summary of how the product catalog is distributed across categories. This will help prioritize category expansion efforts and identify where the assortment may be over- or under-represented.
reference_sql: SELECT CategoryID, COUNT(ProductID) AS ProductCount FROM Products GROUP BY CategoryID ORDER BY ProductCount DESC

question: For each shipper (ShipVia), calculate the total number of orders, the average freight cost, the minimum freight cost, and the maximum freight cost. Only include shippers that have handled more than 50 orders. Order the results by average freight cost in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Logistics wants to evaluate shipper performance and cost efficiency across all fulfilled orders. Specifically, they need a summary of freight costs per shipper to identify which carriers are most expensive on average and how much volume each is handling.
reference_sql: SELECT ShipVia, COUNT(OrderID) AS TotalOrders, ROUND(AVG(Freight), 2) AS AvgFreight, MIN(Freight) AS MinFreight, MAX(Freight) AS MaxFreight FROM Orders GROUP BY ShipVia HAVING COUNT(OrderID) > 50 ORDER BY AvgFreight DESC

question: Using only the Order Details table, calculate the total revenue, average discount, and number of distinct products for each order. Then filter to only include orders where the total revenue (after applying discounts) exceeds 2000. Return the OrderID, total revenue (rounded to 2 decimal places), average discount percentage (rounded to 4 decimal places), and distinct product count, ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants to identify high-value orders to prioritize for a customer loyalty review. She specifically wants to focus on orders where the discounted revenue surpasses $2,000, and needs a breakdown of revenue, average discount applied, and product variety per order to assess deal quality.
reference_sql: SELECT OrderID, ROUND(SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)), 2) AS TotalRevenue, ROUND(AVG(Discount), 4) AS AvgDiscount, COUNT(DISTINCT ProductID) AS DistinctProductCount FROM "Order Details" GROUP BY OrderID HAVING SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) > 2000 ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC

question: For each ship country, calculate the total number of orders, the average freight cost, the minimum freight cost, and the maximum freight cost. Only include countries that have placed more than 5 orders. Order the results by average freight cost in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Logistics wants to understand shipping cost patterns across different destination countries. She needs a summary report to identify which countries have the highest and most variable freight costs so the team can renegotiate shipper rates or adjust pricing strategies.
reference_sql: SELECT ShipCountry, COUNT(OrderID) AS TotalOrders, ROUND(AVG(Freight), 2) AS AvgFreight, MIN(Freight) AS MinFreight, MAX(Freight) AS MaxFreight FROM Orders GROUP BY ShipCountry HAVING COUNT(OrderID) > 5 ORDER BY AvgFreight DESC

question: For each product, calculate the total revenue (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)), the number of distinct orders it appeared in, and the average discount applied. Then, using a window function, rank products within each category by total revenue (highest first). Return only products whose average discount is greater than the overall average discount across all order line items, showing: ProductID, CategoryID (from Products table — note: you must join to get this), total_revenue, order_count, avg_discount, and revenue_rank. Wait — constrain yourself to ONLY the 'Order Details' table for all aggregations and ranking, and use ProductID as a proxy (no join allowed). Rank products by total_revenue descending using DENSE_RANK() partitioned by... the first digit of ProductID (treat CAST((ProductID-1)/10 AS INTEGER) as a pseudo-category bucket). Order results by pseudo_category_bucket ASC, revenue_rank ASC.
business_context: The VP of Merchandising wants to identify top-performing products within product-ID-based buckets (a proxy for category tiers) that are being sold at above-average discount rates. The goal is to flag items driving high revenue despite heavy discounting, which may indicate margin leakage that needs pricing strategy review. This analysis should be derived purely from order line-item data without referencing the product catalog.
reference_sql:
WITH base_agg AS (
    SELECT
        ProductID,
        CAST((ProductID - 1) / 10 AS INTEGER) AS pseudo_category_bucket,
        ROUND(SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity * (1.0 - Discount)), 2) AS total_revenue,
        COUNT(DISTINCT OrderID) AS order_count,
        AVG(Discount) AS avg_discount
    FROM "Order Details"
    GROUP BY ProductID
),
overall_avg AS (
    SELECT AVG(Discount) AS overall_avg_discount
    FROM "Order Details"
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        b.ProductID,
        b.pseudo_category_bucket,
        b.total_revenue,
        b.order_count,
        ROUND(b.avg_discount, 4) AS avg_discount,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY b.pseudo_category_bucket
            ORDER BY b.total_revenue DESC
        ) AS revenue_rank
    FROM base_agg b
    CROSS JOIN overall_avg o
    WHERE b.avg_discount > o.overall_avg_discount
)
SELECT
    ProductID,
    pseudo_category_bucket,
    total_revenue,
    order_count,
    avg_discount,
    revenue_rank
FROM ranked
ORDER BY pseudo_category_bucket ASC, revenue_rank ASC

question: For each year-month, calculate the total number of orders, total freight cost, average freight cost per order, and the cumulative (running total) freight cost ordered by year-month. Additionally, flag each month as 'High' if its total freight is above the overall average monthly freight, otherwise flag it as 'Low'. Return only months where at least 10 orders were placed.
business_context: The VP of Operations wants a longitudinal view of shipping costs to identify seasonal freight spikes and benchmark each month against the historical average. This will inform negotiations with freight carriers and help forecast logistics budgets for the coming year.
reference_sql:
WITH monthly_freight AS (
    SELECT
        STRFTIME('%Y-%m', OrderDate) AS YearMonth,
        COUNT(OrderID) AS TotalOrders,
        ROUND(SUM(Freight), 2) AS TotalFreight,
        ROUND(AVG(Freight), 2) AS AvgFreightPerOrder
    FROM Orders
    GROUP BY STRFTIME('%Y-%m', OrderDate)
    HAVING COUNT(OrderID) >= 10
),
with_running_total AS (
    SELECT
        YearMonth,
        TotalOrders,
        TotalFreight,
        AvgFreightPerOrder,
        ROUND(SUM(TotalFreight) OVER (ORDER BY YearMonth ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS RunningTotalFreight,
        AVG(TotalFreight) OVER () AS OverallAvgMonthlyFreight
    FROM monthly_freight
)
SELECT
    YearMonth,
    TotalOrders,
    TotalFreight,
    AvgFreightPerOrder,
    RunningTotalFreight,
    CASE WHEN TotalFreight > OverallAvgMonthlyFreight THEN 'High' ELSE 'Low' END AS FreightFlag
FROM with_running_total
ORDER BY YearMonth

question: For each year and quarter of order activity, calculate the total number of orders, the average freight cost, the minimum and maximum freight costs, and the percentage of orders that were shipped late (i.e., ShippedDate > RequiredDate). Only include year-quarter combinations with at least 20 orders. Order results by year and quarter ascending.
business_context: The VP of Operations wants a quarterly freight and fulfillment summary to identify seasonal patterns in shipping delays and cost spikes. They need this broken down by year and quarter, focusing only on periods with sufficient order volume to draw meaningful conclusions.
reference_sql:
SELECT
  STRFTIME('%Y', OrderDate) AS OrderYear,
  CAST(((STRFTIME('%m', OrderDate) - 1) / 3) + 1 AS TEXT) AS OrderQuarter,
  COUNT(OrderID) AS TotalOrders,
  ROUND(AVG(Freight), 2) AS AvgFreight,
  MIN(Freight) AS MinFreight,
  MAX(Freight) AS MaxFreight,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN ShippedDate > RequiredDate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(OrderID),
    2
  ) AS PctLateShipments
FROM Orders
WHERE OrderDate IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  STRFTIME('%Y', OrderDate),
  CAST(((STRFTIME('%m', OrderDate) - 1) / 3) + 1 AS TEXT)
HAVING COUNT(OrderID) >= 20
ORDER BY
  OrderYear ASC,
  OrderQuarter ASC

question: Find all customers who have placed more than 10 orders. Return the CustomerID and the total number of orders they have placed, ordered by order count descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-frequency buyers to target for a new loyalty program. Specifically, they need a list of customers who have placed more than 10 orders so the team can prioritize outreach efforts.
reference_sql: SELECT CustomerID, COUNT(OrderID) AS TotalOrders FROM Orders GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(OrderID) > 10 ORDER BY TotalOrders DESC

question: Find all customers who have placed more than 10 orders. Return the CustomerID and the total number of orders they have placed.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-frequency buyers for a new loyalty rewards program. Any customer with more than 10 orders should be flagged as a priority account for the account management team.
reference_sql: SELECT CustomerID, COUNT(OrderID) AS TotalOrders FROM Orders GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(OrderID) > 10

question: Find all customers who have placed more than 10 orders. Return the CustomerID and the total number of orders they have placed, ordered by order count descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-frequency buyers for a new loyalty program. Customers who have placed more than 10 orders are considered 'VIP' accounts and should be targeted with exclusive wholesale discounts.
reference_sql: SELECT CustomerID, COUNT(OrderID) AS TotalOrders FROM Orders GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(OrderID) > 10 ORDER BY TotalOrders DESC

question: Identify all customers who have placed more than 10 orders and whose average freight cost per order exceeds $50. Return the customer ID, company name, total number of orders, and their average freight cost rounded to 2 decimal places.
business_context: The Head of Logistics wants to identify high-volume customers with above-average shipping costs to evaluate whether they qualify for a freight discount program. Understanding which customers drive both order volume and freight expenses will help prioritize contract renegotiations with shipping carriers.
reference_sql: SELECT o.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS TotalOrders, ROUND(AVG(o.Freight), 2) AS AvgFreight FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID GROUP BY o.CustomerID, c.CompanyName HAVING COUNT(o.OrderID) > 10 AND AVG(o.Freight) > 50 ORDER BY AvgFreight DESC

question: Identify all customers who have placed more than 10 orders and have a total freight cost exceeding $500 across all their orders. Return the customer ID, company name, total number of orders, and total freight cost, ordered by total freight cost descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales Operations wants to identify high-frequency, high-shipping-cost customers to evaluate whether they qualify for a freight discount program. Understanding which customers consistently generate large shipping expenses will help prioritize contract renegotiations with logistics partners.
reference_sql: SELECT o.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS TotalOrders, SUM(o.Freight) AS TotalFreight FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID GROUP BY o.CustomerID, c.CompanyName HAVING COUNT(o.OrderID) > 10 AND SUM(o.Freight) > 500 ORDER BY TotalFreight DESC

question: Identify all customers who have placed more than 10 orders in total, along with their total number of orders and the total freight cost across all their orders. Return the results sorted by total freight cost in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-frequency customers for a VIP loyalty program. Specifically, they need a list of customers who have placed more than 10 orders so the account management team can prioritize outreach and offer preferential shipping rates.
reference_sql: SELECT c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS TotalOrders, ROUND(SUM(o.Freight), 2) AS TotalFreight FROM Customers c JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName HAVING COUNT(o.OrderID) > 10 ORDER BY TotalFreight DESC

question: Identify customers who have placed at least 5 orders where the average order value (sum of UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount) per order) exceeds $500, and whose total freight costs across all their orders is greater than $100. Return the CustomerID, CompanyName, number of qualifying orders, average order value rounded to 2 decimal places, and total freight cost rounded to 2 decimal places. Order results by average order value descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-value, high-frequency customers for a new VIP loyalty program. Specifically, they need customers who consistently place large orders and also generate significant shipping revenue, as these accounts represent the most profitable relationships to nurture.
reference_sql:
WITH OrderValues AS (
    SELECT
        o.OrderID,
        o.CustomerID,
        o.Freight,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS OrderValue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.CustomerID, o.Freight
)
SELECT
    ov.CustomerID,
    c.CompanyName,
    COUNT(ov.OrderID) AS NumOrders,
    ROUND(AVG(ov.OrderValue), 2) AS AvgOrderValue,
    ROUND(SUM(ov.Freight), 2) AS TotalFreight
FROM OrderValues ov
JOIN Customers c ON ov.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
GROUP BY ov.CustomerID, c.CompanyName
HAVING COUNT(ov.OrderID) >= 5
    AND AVG(ov.OrderValue) > 500
    AND SUM(ov.Freight) > 100
ORDER BY AvgOrderValue DESC

question: Identify customers who have placed at least 5 orders where the average order value (sum of UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount) per order) exceeds $500. For each such customer, return their CompanyName, total number of qualifying orders, and their overall average order value rounded to 2 decimal places. Order the results by overall average order value descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-value, high-frequency customers for a new VIP loyalty program. Specifically, they need customers who consistently place large orders — defined as those with at least 5 orders and an average order value above $500 — so the sales team can prioritize account management resources.
reference_sql:
WITH OrderValues AS (
    SELECT
        o.OrderID,
        o.CustomerID,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS OrderValue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.CustomerID
)
SELECT
    c.CompanyName,
    COUNT(ov.OrderID) AS TotalOrders,
    ROUND(AVG(ov.OrderValue), 2) AS AvgOrderValue
FROM OrderValues ov
JOIN Customers c ON ov.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
GROUP BY ov.CustomerID, c.CompanyName
HAVING COUNT(ov.OrderID) >= 5 AND AVG(ov.OrderValue) > 500
ORDER BY AvgOrderValue DESC

question: Identify customers who have placed at least 5 orders where the average order value (sum of UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount) per order) exceeds $500, and whose total freight cost across all their orders is greater than $200. Return the CustomerID, CompanyName, total number of orders, average order value rounded to 2 decimal places, and total freight cost rounded to 2 decimal places. Order the results by average order value descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales at Northwind Traders wants to identify high-value, high-engagement customers for a new premium loyalty program. Specifically, they need customers who consistently place sizable orders (average order value above $500) and have accumulated meaningful shipping costs (total freight > $200), with enough order history (at least 5 orders) to be considered reliable buyers.
reference_sql:
WITH OrderValues AS (
    SELECT
        o.OrderID,
        o.CustomerID,
        o.Freight,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS OrderValue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.CustomerID, o.Freight
),
CustomerStats AS (
    SELECT
        ov.CustomerID,
        COUNT(ov.OrderID) AS TotalOrders,
        ROUND(AVG(ov.OrderValue), 2) AS AvgOrderValue,
        ROUND(SUM(ov.Freight), 2) AS TotalFreight
    FROM OrderValues ov
    GROUP BY ov.CustomerID
    HAVING COUNT(ov.OrderID) >= 5
        AND AVG(ov.OrderValue) > 500
        AND SUM(ov.Freight) > 200
)
SELECT
    cs.CustomerID,
    c.CompanyName,
    cs.TotalOrders,
    cs.AvgOrderValue,
    cs.TotalFreight
FROM CustomerStats cs
JOIN Customers c ON cs.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
ORDER BY cs.AvgOrderValue DESC;

question: Using a CTE, calculate the total revenue (UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) for each customer, then return the CustomerID and their total revenue, ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants a quick summary of total revenue generated by each customer to identify the top spenders. This will help prioritize the key accounts for the upcoming quarterly business review.
reference_sql:
WITH CustomerRevenue AS (
  SELECT
    o.CustomerID,
    SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS TotalRevenue
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.CustomerID
)
SELECT
  CustomerID,
  ROUND(TotalRevenue, 2) AS TotalRevenue
FROM CustomerRevenue
ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC;

question: Using a CTE, calculate the total number of orders placed by each customer. Return the customer's CompanyName, their CustomerID, and their total order count, ordered by total orders descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants a quick summary of customer engagement to identify the most active buyers. She needs a clean, readable query using a CTE so the analytics team can easily maintain and extend it in the future.
reference_sql:
WITH CustomerOrderCounts AS (
    SELECT
        CustomerID,
        COUNT(OrderID) AS TotalOrders
    FROM Orders
    GROUP BY CustomerID
)
SELECT
    c.CompanyName,
    c.CustomerID,
    coc.TotalOrders
FROM Customers c
JOIN CustomerOrderCounts coc ON c.CustomerID = coc.CustomerID
ORDER BY coc.TotalOrders DESC;

question: Using a CTE, calculate the total revenue (UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) for each customer, then return only the customers whose total revenue exceeds $10,000. Display the CustomerID and their total revenue, ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-value customers who have generated more than $10,000 in total revenue across all their orders. This will help prioritize account management efforts and tailor loyalty programs for top-spending clients.
reference_sql:
WITH CustomerRevenue AS (
  SELECT
    o.CustomerID,
    SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS TotalRevenue
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.CustomerID
)
SELECT
  CustomerID,
  ROUND(TotalRevenue, 2) AS TotalRevenue
FROM CustomerRevenue
WHERE TotalRevenue > 10000
ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC;

question: Using a CTE, calculate the total revenue (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)) per customer, then return only the customers whose total revenue exceeds the average total revenue across all customers. Include the customer's company name, country, and their total revenue rounded to 2 decimal places, ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-value customers who spend above average so the account management team can prioritize relationship-building efforts and tailor promotional offers. They need a clean list of these customers along with their country and total spend.
reference_sql:
WITH CustomerRevenue AS (
    SELECT
        o.CustomerID,
        c.CompanyName,
        c.Country,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
    GROUP BY o.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, c.Country
)
SELECT
    CustomerID,
    CompanyName,
    Country,
    TotalRevenue
FROM CustomerRevenue
WHERE TotalRevenue > (SELECT AVG(TotalRevenue) FROM CustomerRevenue)
ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC;

question: Using a CTE, identify all customers whose total order revenue (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)) exceeds the average total order revenue across all customers. Return the customer's company name, their total revenue, and the overall average revenue, rounded to 2 decimal places.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-value customers who are spending above the company average so the account management team can prioritize them for a new loyalty program. They need a clear comparison of each customer's total spend against the overall average.
reference_sql:
WITH CustomerRevenue AS (
    SELECT
        o.CustomerID,
        c.CompanyName,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
    GROUP BY o.CustomerID, c.CompanyName
),
AvgRevenue AS (
    SELECT ROUND(AVG(TotalRevenue), 2) AS AvgCustomerRevenue
    FROM CustomerRevenue
)
SELECT
    cr.CompanyName,
    cr.TotalRevenue,
    ar.AvgCustomerRevenue
FROM CustomerRevenue cr
CROSS JOIN AvgRevenue ar
WHERE cr.TotalRevenue > ar.AvgCustomerRevenue
ORDER BY cr.TotalRevenue DESC;

question: Using a CTE, identify customers whose total order revenue (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)) exceeds the average total order revenue across all customers. Return the customer's company name, their total revenue, and the overall average revenue, rounded to 2 decimal places.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-value customers who are spending above the company average so they can be targeted for a premium loyalty program. She needs a clear comparison of each qualifying customer's spend against the overall customer average.
reference_sql:
WITH CustomerRevenue AS (
    SELECT
        o.CustomerID,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    GROUP BY o.CustomerID
),
AvgRevenue AS (
    SELECT AVG(TotalRevenue) AS AvgCustomerRevenue
    FROM CustomerRevenue
)
SELECT
    c.CompanyName,
    ROUND(cr.TotalRevenue, 2) AS TotalRevenue,
    ROUND(ar.AvgCustomerRevenue, 2) AS AvgCustomerRevenue
FROM CustomerRevenue cr
JOIN Customers c ON cr.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
CROSS JOIN AvgRevenue ar
WHERE cr.TotalRevenue > ar.AvgCustomerRevenue
ORDER BY cr.TotalRevenue DESC

question: For each product category, identify the top 2 customers (by total revenue) and calculate what percentage of that category's overall revenue they account for. Return the category name, customer company name, their total revenue for that category, and their percentage share of the category's total revenue. Order results by category name and revenue percentage descending.
business_context: The VP of Sales wants to understand revenue concentration risk across product categories. She needs to know which key accounts dominate each category so the sales team can prioritize relationship management and identify categories where revenue is dangerously dependent on just one or two customers.
reference_sql:
WITH CustomerCategoryRevenue AS (
    SELECT
        c.CategoryID,
        c.CategoryName,
        cu.CustomerID,
        cu.CompanyName,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Categories c
    JOIN Products p ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
    JOIN Orders o ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
    JOIN Customers cu ON o.CustomerID = cu.CustomerID
    GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName, cu.CustomerID, cu.CompanyName
),
CategoryTotals AS (
    SELECT
        CategoryID,
        SUM(TotalRevenue) AS CategoryTotalRevenue
    FROM CustomerCategoryRevenue
    GROUP BY CategoryID
),
RankedCustomers AS (
    SELECT
        ccr.CategoryName,
        ccr.CompanyName,
        ccr.TotalRevenue,
        ct.CategoryTotalRevenue,
        ROUND(ccr.TotalRevenue * 100.0 / ct.CategoryTotalRevenue, 2) AS RevenuePercentage,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ccr.CategoryID ORDER BY ccr.TotalRevenue DESC) AS RevenueRank
    FROM CustomerCategoryRevenue ccr
    JOIN CategoryTotals ct ON ccr.CategoryID = ct.CategoryID
)
SELECT
    CategoryName,
    CompanyName,
    ROUND(TotalRevenue, 2) AS TotalRevenue,
    RevenuePercentage
FROM RankedCustomers
WHERE RevenueRank <= 2
ORDER BY CategoryName, RevenuePercentage DESC

question: Rank all products by their unit price from highest to lowest using DENSE_RANK. Return the product name, unit price, and the dense rank. Order the results by rank ascending.

question: For each product category, identify the top 2 most expensive products (by unit price) that are not discontinued. Return the category name, product name, unit price, and their rank within the category. If two products share the same price, they should receive the same rank.
business_context: The Head of Merchandising wants to spotlight premium products in each category for an upcoming trade catalog. She needs the top 2 highest-priced active products per category, with tied prices ranked equally, to ensure accurate featured product listings.
reference_sql:
WITH ranked_products AS (
  SELECT
    c.CategoryName,
    p.ProductName,
    p.UnitPrice,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.CategoryID ORDER BY p.UnitPrice DESC) AS price_rank
  FROM Products p
  JOIN Categories c ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID

)

FROM ranked_products

question: For each product category, identify the top 2 products by total revenue (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)). question: For each customer, list their orders in chronological order and show the number of days elapsed between their current order and their previous order. Include the CustomerID, OrderID, OrderDate, the previous order date, and the gap in days. Only include rows where a previous order exists (i.e., exclude each customer's first order).
business_context: The Head of Customer Success wants to understand ordering frequency patterns across Northwind's customer base. Specifically, she wants to identify customers with unusually long gaps between orders, which may indicate churn risk or seasonal buying behavior.
reference_sql:
WITH OrderedOrders AS (
    SELECT
        CustomerID,
        OrderID,
        OrderDate,
        LAG(OrderDate) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY OrderDate) AS PrevOrderDate
    FROM Orders
)
SELECT
    CustomerID,
    OrderID,
    OrderDate,
    PrevOrderDate,
    CAST(JULIANDAY(OrderDate) - JULIANDAY(PrevOrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS DaysSincePrevOrder
FROM OrderedOrders
WHERE PrevOrderDate IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY CustomerID, OrderDate

question: For each customer, calculate the revenue from their most recent order and the revenue from their previous order, then compute the difference between them. Revenue for an order is defined as the sum of (UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) across all order line items. Return the CustomerID, CompanyName, the most recent OrderDate, the current order revenue, the previous order revenue, and the revenue change (current minus previous). Only include customers who have placed at least two orders.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify customers whose spending is trending up or down. By comparing each customer's latest order value to their previous one, the team can prioritize outreach to customers showing a significant revenue decline before they churn.
reference_sql:
WITH order_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        o.CustomerID,
        o.OrderID,
        o.OrderDate,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS order_total
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    GROUP BY o.CustomerID, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate
),
order_with_lag AS (
    SELECT
        CustomerID,
        OrderID,
        OrderDate,
        order_total,
        LAG(order_total) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY OrderDate) AS prev_order_total,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY OrderDate DESC) AS rn
    FROM order_revenue
)
SELECT
    owl.CustomerID,
    c.CompanyName,
    owl.OrderDate AS latest_order_date,
    ROUND(owl.order_total, 2) AS current_order_revenue,
    ROUND(owl.prev_order_total, 2) AS previous_order_revenue,
    ROUND(owl.order_total - owl.prev_order_total, 2) AS revenue_change
FROM order_with_lag owl
JOIN Customers c ON owl.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
WHERE owl.rn = 1
  AND owl.prev_order_total IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY revenue_change ASC

question: For each customer, retrieve their orders sorted by OrderDate and show the current order's freight cost alongside the previous order's freight cost. Calculate the difference between the current and previous freight costs. Only include rows where a previous order exists (i.e., it is not the customer's first order).
business_context: The Head of Logistics wants to understand how shipping costs are trending for repeat customers over time. By comparing each order's freight cost to the prior order for the same customer, the team can flag unusual spikes or drops in shipping expenses and investigate potential carrier inefficiencies.
reference_sql:
WITH order_freight AS (
    SELECT
        CustomerID,
        OrderID,
        OrderDate,
        Freight,
        LAG(Freight) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY OrderDate) AS prev_freight
    FROM Orders
)
SELECT
    CustomerID,
    OrderID,
    OrderDate,
    Freight AS current_freight,
    prev_freight,
    ROUND(Freight - prev_freight, 2) AS freight_difference
FROM order_freight
WHERE prev_freight IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY CustomerID, OrderDate;

question: For each customer, calculate the month-over-month revenue change using LAG. For every month in which a customer placed orders, compute their total revenue (sum of UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)), the previous month's total revenue, the absolute change, and classify the trend as 'Growth', 'Decline', or 'Flat'. Only include customers who have placed orders in at least 3 distinct months. Return the CustomerID, CompanyName, order month (formatted as YYYY-MM), current month revenue, previous month revenue, revenue change, and trend classification. Order by CustomerID and order month.
business_context: The VP of Sales wants to identify which customers are consistently growing their spend with Northwind Traders versus those whose purchasing is declining month over month. The analysis will be used to prioritize the sales team's account management efforts and flag at-risk accounts for intervention before the end of the fiscal quarter.
reference_sql:
WITH monthly_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        o.CustomerID,
        c.CompanyName,
        STRFTIME('%Y-%m', o.OrderDate) AS order_month,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS total_revenue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
    GROUP BY o.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, STRFTIME('%Y-%m', o.OrderDate)
),
customer_month_counts AS (
    SELECT CustomerID
    FROM monthly_revenue
    GROUP BY CustomerID
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT order_month) >= 3
),
lagged_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        mr.CustomerID,
        mr.CompanyName,
        mr.order_month,
        mr.total_revenue AS current_revenue,
        LAG(mr.total_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY mr.CustomerID ORDER BY mr.order_month) AS prev_revenue
    FROM monthly_revenue mr
    INNER JOIN customer_month_counts cmc ON mr.CustomerID = cmc.CustomerID
)
SELECT
    CustomerID,
    CompanyName,
    order_month,
    current_revenue,
    prev_revenue,
    ROUND(current_revenue - COALESCE(prev_revenue, 0), 2) AS revenue_change,
    CASE
        WHEN prev_revenue IS NULL THEN 'N/A'
        WHEN current_revenue > prev_revenue THEN 'Growth'
        WHEN current_revenue < prev_revenue THEN 'Decline'
        ELSE 'Flat'
    END AS trend
FROM lagged_revenue
ORDER BY CustomerID, order_month

question: For each customer, calculate their monthly order revenue and identify months where their revenue declined compared to the previous month. Return the customer ID, company name, the year-month, the current month's revenue, the previous month's revenue, and the revenue change (current minus previous). Only include rows where a previous month exists and the revenue declined (i.e., the change is negative). Order results by the revenue change ascending (largest declines first).
business_context: The Head of Sales at Northwind Traders wants to proactively identify customers who are spending less than they did the prior month, so the account management team can reach out and prevent churn. They need a ranked list of the sharpest month-over-month revenue declines by customer.
reference_sql:
WITH monthly_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        o.CustomerID,
        c.CompanyName,
        STRFTIME('%Y-%m', o.OrderDate) AS year_month,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS revenue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
    GROUP BY o.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, year_month
),
revenue_with_lag AS (
    SELECT
        CustomerID,
        CompanyName,
        year_month,
        revenue AS current_revenue,
        LAG(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY year_month) AS prev_revenue
    FROM monthly_revenue
)
SELECT
    CustomerID,
    CompanyName,
    year_month,
    current_revenue,
    prev_revenue,
    ROUND(current_revenue - prev_revenue, 2) AS revenue_change
FROM revenue_with_lag
WHERE prev_revenue IS NOT NULL
  AND current_revenue < prev_revenue
ORDER BY revenue_change ASC;

question: For each customer, calculate the month-over-month change in their total order revenue. Return the customer ID, company name, order month (formatted as YYYY-MM), total revenue for that month, the previous month's revenue, and the absolute revenue change. Only include rows where a previous month exists. Order results by company name and order month.
business_context: The Head of Sales at Northwind Traders wants to identify which customers are showing significant growth or decline in their purchasing behavior on a month-by-month basis. This analysis will inform the account management team on where to focus retention and upsell efforts for the upcoming quarter.
reference_sql:
WITH monthly_revenue AS (
    SELECT

        c.CompanyName,
        STRFTIME('%Y-%m', o.OrderDate) AS order_month,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS total_revenue
    FROM Customers c
    JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, order_month
),
lagged_revenue AS (
    SELECT

        CompanyName,
        order_month,

question: Write a query that shows each order date and the running total of freight costs over time. For each order, display the OrderID, OrderDate, Freight, and the cumulative sum of Freight ordered by OrderDate and OrderID.
business_context: The Head of Logistics wants to monitor how shipping costs accumulate over time. By tracking a running total of freight charges, the team can identify periods of high shipping spend and plan budget allocations accordingly.
reference_sql: SELECT OrderID, OrderDate, Freight, SUM(Freight) OVER (ORDER BY OrderDate, OrderID) AS RunningTotalFreight FROM Orders ORDER BY OrderDate, OrderID;

question: Write a query that shows each order date and the running total of freight costs over time. For each order, display the OrderID, OrderDate, Freight, and the cumulative sum of Freight ordered by OrderDate ascending.
business_context: The Head of Logistics asks: 'I need to understand how our shipping costs have been accumulating over time. Can you give me a running total of freight charges across all orders, sorted by order date, so I can spot periods of rapid cost growth?'
reference_sql: SELECT OrderID, OrderDate, Freight, SUM(Freight) OVER (ORDER BY OrderDate ASC) AS RunningTotalFreight FROM Orders ORDER BY OrderDate ASC;

question: Write a query that shows each order date and the running total of freight costs over time. For each order (ordered by OrderDate), display the OrderID, OrderDate, Freight, and the cumulative sum of Freight up to and including that order.
business_context: The Head of Logistics wants to track how freight expenses accumulate over time to better forecast shipping budgets. They need a simple report showing the running total of freight costs as orders are placed chronologically.
reference_sql: SELECT OrderID, OrderDate, Freight, SUM(Freight) OVER (ORDER BY OrderDate, OrderID) AS RunningFreightTotal FROM Orders ORDER BY OrderDate, OrderID

question: Write a query that calculates the monthly revenue for 2017 along with a running total of revenue accumulated from the start of the year through each month. Monthly revenue should be calculated as the sum of (UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) from Order Details, joined to Orders filtered to the year 2017. Return the month number, the monthly revenue, and the running total revenue, ordered by month.
business_context: The VP of Sales wants to track how cumulative revenue builds throughout 2017 to evaluate whether the company is on pace to hit its annual revenue target. She needs a month-by-month view showing both the individual month's revenue and the year-to-date running total so she can spot slowdowns early.
reference_sql:
WITH monthly_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(strftime('%m', o.OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS Month,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS MonthlyRevenue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2017'
    GROUP BY strftime('%m', o.OrderDate)
)
SELECT
    Month,
    MonthlyRevenue,
    ROUND(SUM(MonthlyRevenue) OVER (ORDER BY Month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS RunningTotalRevenue
FROM monthly_revenue
ORDER BY Month;

question: Write a query that calculates the monthly revenue for each year-month and the running total of revenue accumulated up to and including that month. Monthly revenue should be calculated as the sum of (UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) from Order Details, joined to Orders using OrderDate. Return the year-month label, monthly revenue, and the running total, ordered chronologically.
business_context: The Head of Finance at Northwind Traders wants to track how cumulative revenue has grown over time. They need a month-by-month breakdown showing both the revenue generated in each individual month and a running total so they can quickly identify milestone periods and overall revenue trajectory.
reference_sql:
WITH monthly_revenue AS (
  SELECT
    strftime('%Y-%m', o.OrderDate) AS year_month,
    ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS monthly_revenue
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%m', o.OrderDate)
)
SELECT
  year_month,
  monthly_revenue,
  ROUND(SUM(monthly_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year_month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS running_total
FROM monthly_revenue
ORDER BY year_month;

question: Write a query that calculates the monthly revenue for 2017 along with a running total of revenue accumulated from January through each month. Monthly revenue should be calculated as the sum of (UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) from Order Details, joined to Orders filtered to the year 2017. Display the month number, monthly revenue (rounded to 2 decimal places), and the cumulative running total (rounded to 2 decimal places), ordered chronologically.
business_context: The Head of Finance wants to track how Northwind's revenue builds up across the calendar year 2017. She needs a month-by-month view showing not just what was earned each month, but the cumulative total to date so she can compare actual performance against annual targets at any point in the year.
reference_sql:
WITH monthly_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(strftime('%m', o.OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS order_month,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS monthly_revenue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2017'
    GROUP BY order_month
)
SELECT
    order_month,
    monthly_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(monthly_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS running_total
FROM monthly_revenue
ORDER BY order_month;

question: For each month in 2017, calculate the total revenue generated, the 3-month rolling average revenue (current month plus the two preceding months), and the cumulative year-to-date revenue. Revenue for each order line is defined as UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount). Return the month number, monthly revenue, 3-month rolling average, and cumulative YTD revenue, ordered by month.
business_context: The CFO of Northwind Traders wants a monthly revenue trend report for 2017 to present to the board. She specifically needs a smoothed rolling average to filter out month-to-month noise, as well as a running year-to-date total to track progress against the annual revenue target.
reference_sql:
WITH monthly_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(strftime('%m', o.OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS month_num,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS monthly_revenue
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2017'
    GROUP BY strftime('%m', o.OrderDate)
)
SELECT
    month_num,
    monthly_revenue,
    ROUND(
        AVG(monthly_revenue) OVER (
            ORDER BY month_num
            ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ), 2
    ) AS rolling_3mo_avg_revenue,
    ROUND(
        SUM(monthly_revenue) OVER (
            ORDER BY month_num
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ), 2
    ) AS ytd_cumulative_revenue
FROM monthly_revenue
ORDER BY month_num

question: For each customer, calculate the cumulative (running) total revenue they have generated over time, ordered by their order dates. The output should show the customer's company name, each order date, the revenue from that specific order, and the running total revenue up to and including that order. Only include orders where the order has actually been shipped. Revenue for each order should be calculated as the sum of (UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) across all order line items.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants to identify which customers have been consistently high-value over time versus those who made a single large purchase. She needs a report showing the cumulative spend per customer across all their shipped orders so the sales team can prioritize retention outreach and spot customers whose spending trajectory is plateauing or declining.
reference_sql:
WITH order_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        o.CustomerID,
        o.OrderID,
        o.OrderDate,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1.0 - od.Discount)) AS order_total
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    WHERE o.ShippedDate IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY o.CustomerID, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate
),
cumulative_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        or1.CustomerID,
        or1.OrderID,
        or1.OrderDate,
        or1.order_total,
        SUM(or1.order_total) OVER (
            PARTITION BY or1.CustomerID
            ORDER BY or1.OrderDate, or1.OrderID
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS running_total_revenue
    FROM order_revenue or1
)
SELECT
    c.CompanyName,
    cr.OrderDate,
    ROUND(cr.order_total, 2) AS order_revenue,
    ROUND(cr.running_total_revenue, 2) AS running_total_revenue
FROM cumulative_revenue cr
JOIN Customers c ON cr.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
ORDER BY c.CompanyName, cr.OrderDate, cr.OrderID

question: List all products along with their category name. Return the product name, unit price, and category name for all products.
business_context: The Head of Merchandising wants a simple product catalog report that shows which category each product belongs to. This will be used to organize the product listing on the company's internal portal.
reference_sql: SELECT p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice, c.CategoryName FROM Products p JOIN Categories c ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID ORDER BY c.CategoryName, p.ProductName;

question: List all products along with their category name. Return the product name, unit price, and category name for every product in the database.
business_context: The Head of Merchandising wants a consolidated product catalog that includes the category each product belongs to. This will be used to build a summary report for the upcoming supplier review meeting.
reference_sql: SELECT p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice, c.CategoryName FROM Products p JOIN Categories c ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID

question: List each product name along with its category name. Return only the product name and category name, sorted alphabetically by category name and then by product name.
business_context: The merchandising team at Northwind Traders wants a simple reference list of all products organized by their category. The Head of Merchandising has requested this to help onboard new sales staff who need to quickly understand what product categories the company carries.
reference_sql: SELECT p.ProductName, c.CategoryName FROM Products p JOIN Categories c ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID ORDER BY c.CategoryName, p.ProductName;

question: For each product category, calculate the total revenue generated (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)) across all orders. Return the category name, the number of distinct products sold, and the total revenue rounded to 2 decimal places. Order the results by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Merchandising wants to understand which product categories are driving the most revenue across all fulfilled orders. This will help inform upcoming supplier negotiations and inventory investment decisions for next quarter.
reference_sql: SELECT c.CategoryName, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ProductID) AS distinct_products_sold, ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS total_revenue FROM Categories c JOIN Products p ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID JOIN "Order Details" od ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName ORDER BY total_revenue DESC

question: List each product's name, its category name, and the supplier's company name, along with the product's current unit price and whether it is discontinued. Only include products that belong to the 'Beverages' or 'Seafood' categories. Order the results by category name and then by product name.
business_context: The Head of Procurement wants a consolidated view of all Beverage and Seafood products to review supplier relationships and pricing ahead of the next contract negotiation cycle. They need to see the product name, category, supplier, current price, and discontinuation status in a single report.
reference_sql: SELECT p.ProductName, c.CategoryName, s.CompanyName AS SupplierName, p.UnitPrice, p.Discontinued FROM Products p JOIN Categories c ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID JOIN Suppliers s ON p.SupplierID = s.SupplierID WHERE c.CategoryName IN ('Beverages', 'Seafood') ORDER BY c.CategoryName, p.ProductName

question: For each product category, calculate the total revenue generated (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)), the number of distinct orders, and the number of distinct products sold. Return the results sorted by total revenue in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Sales at Northwind Traders wants a category-level performance summary to decide which product lines to prioritize in the upcoming trade catalog. She needs to understand which categories drive the most revenue and order volume across all historical transactions.
reference_sql: SELECT c.CategoryName, ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS TotalRevenue, COUNT(DISTINCT od.OrderID) AS DistinctOrders, COUNT(DISTINCT od.ProductID) AS DistinctProducts FROM Categories c JOIN Products p ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID JOIN "Order Details" od ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC

question: For each product category, identify the top-performing employee (by total revenue generated) and include details about both. Return the category name, the employee's full name, their title, the total revenue they generated in that category (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)), and their rank within the category. Only include the #1 ranked employee per category.
business_context: The VP of Sales wants to recognize category champions — the single best-performing employee in each product category based on net revenue. This will be used in the upcoming quarterly review to assign category ownership and bonus allocations. Please include employee title and category details for the full report.
reference_sql:
WITH CategoryEmployeeRevenue AS (
    SELECT
        c.CategoryID,
        c.CategoryName,
        e.EmployeeID,
        e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS EmployeeFullName,
        e.Title AS EmployeeTitle,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Categories c
    JOIN Products p ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.ProductID = p.ProductID
    JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
    GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName, e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName, e.Title
),
RankedEmployees AS (
    SELECT
        CategoryID,
        CategoryName,
        EmployeeID,
        EmployeeFullName,
        EmployeeTitle,
        TotalRevenue,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY CategoryID ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC) AS RevenueRank
    FROM CategoryEmployeeRevenue
)
SELECT
    CategoryName,
    EmployeeFullName,
    EmployeeTitle,
    TotalRevenue,
    RevenueRank
FROM RankedEmployees
WHERE RevenueRank = 1
ORDER BY CategoryName;

question: For each product category, identify the top-performing employee (by total revenue generated) along with the total number of distinct customers they served and the total revenue they generated within that category. Total revenue for a line item is calculated as UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount). Return the CategoryName, employee's full name, total revenue (rounded to 2 decimal places), and distinct customer count. In case of a tie in revenue within a category, pick the employee with the higher distinct customer count.
business_context: The VP of Sales wants to understand which sales representatives are dominating each product category. This analysis will inform upcoming territory realignments and help leadership reward top performers with category-specific bonuses heading into the next quarter.
reference_sql:
WITH CategoryEmployeeRevenue AS (
    SELECT
        c.CategoryID,
        c.CategoryName,
        e.EmployeeID,
        e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS EmployeeName,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS TotalRevenue,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.CustomerID) AS DistinctCustomers
    FROM Categories c
    JOIN Products p ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.ProductID = p.ProductID
    JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
    GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName, e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName
),
Ranked AS (
    SELECT
        CategoryID,
        CategoryName,
        EmployeeName,
        TotalRevenue,
        DistinctCustomers,
        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY CategoryID
            ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC, DistinctCustomers DESC
        ) AS rnk
    FROM CategoryEmployeeRevenue
)
SELECT
    CategoryName,
    EmployeeName,
    TotalRevenue,
    DistinctCustomers
FROM Ranked
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY CategoryName;

question: For each product category, identify the top-performing employee (by total revenue generated) and show the category name, employee full name, number of distinct orders they handled containing products in that category, total revenue they generated for that category (unit price × quantity × (1 - discount)), and their rank within the category. Only include categories where at least 3 distinct employees have handled orders.
business_context: The VP of Sales wants to identify category champions — the best-performing sales rep in each product category — to assign as dedicated category specialists. This analysis will inform the upcoming territory restructuring and incentive compensation plan for Q3.
reference_sql:
WITH category_employee_stats AS (
    SELECT
        c.CategoryID,
        c.CategoryName,
        e.EmployeeID,
        e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS EmployeeFullName,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.OrderID) AS DistinctOrders,
        ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Categories c
    JOIN Products p ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
    JOIN Orders o ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
    JOIN Employees e ON o.EmployeeID = e.EmployeeID
    GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName, e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName
),
category_employee_counts AS (
    SELECT
        CategoryID,
        COUNT(DISTINCT EmployeeID) AS NumEmployees
    FROM category_employee_stats
    GROUP BY CategoryID
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT EmployeeID) >= 3
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        ces.CategoryName,
        ces.EmployeeFullName,
        ces.DistinctOrders,
        ces.TotalRevenue,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ces.CategoryID ORDER BY ces.TotalRevenue DESC) AS RevenueRank
    FROM category_employee_stats ces
    JOIN category_employee_counts cec ON ces.CategoryID = cec.CategoryID
)
SELECT
    CategoryName,
    EmployeeFullName,
    DistinctOrders,
    TotalRevenue,
    RevenueRank
FROM ranked
WHERE RevenueRank = 1
ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC

question: Write a query that returns each product's name, unit price, and the average unit price of all products in the same category. Use a correlated subquery to calculate the category average. Only include products where the product's unit price is above the average for its category.
business_context: The Head of Merchandising wants to identify premium-priced products within each category — specifically those priced above the category average. This will help the team understand which products command a price premium and may warrant additional marketing focus.
reference_sql: SELECT p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice, p.CategoryID, (SELECT AVG(p2.UnitPrice) FROM Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID) AS AvgCategoryPrice FROM Products p WHERE p.UnitPrice > (SELECT AVG(p3.UnitPrice) FROM Products p3 WHERE p3.CategoryID = p.CategoryID) ORDER BY p.CategoryID, p.UnitPrice DESC

question: Write a query to retrieve each product's name and unit price, but only include products whose unit price is above the average unit price of all products in the same category. Use a correlated subquery to calculate the average unit price per category.
business_context: The Head of Merchandising wants to identify premium-priced products within each category to highlight them in the upcoming wholesale catalog. She needs a list of products that are priced above the average for their respective category so the sales team can position them as premium offerings.
reference_sql: SELECT p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice, p.CategoryID FROM Products p WHERE p.UnitPrice > (SELECT AVG(p2.UnitPrice) FROM Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID) ORDER BY p.CategoryID, p.UnitPrice DESC

question: Write a query to retrieve all products whose unit price is above the average unit price of all products in the same category. Return the product name, category ID, and unit price.
business_context: The Head of Merchandising wants to identify premium-priced products within each category to review pricing strategy. They need a list of products that are priced above the average for their respective category so the team can evaluate whether those products are appropriately positioned in the market.
reference_sql: SELECT ProductName, CategoryID, UnitPrice FROM Products p WHERE UnitPrice > (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) FROM Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID)

question: For each customer, retrieve their CompanyName, ContactName, and the total number of orders they have placed. Only include customers whose total order count is greater than the average number of orders placed per customer across all customers. Order results by order count descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify the most active buyers for a new loyalty program. She needs a list of customers who order more frequently than the typical customer, so the team can prioritize outreach and exclusive offers.
reference_sql: SELECT c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, c.ContactName, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount FROM Customers c JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, c.ContactName HAVING COUNT(o.OrderID) > ( SELECT AVG(CustomerOrderCount) FROM ( SELECT COUNT(OrderID) AS CustomerOrderCount FROM Orders GROUP BY CustomerID ) AS subq ) ORDER BY OrderCount DESC

question: For each customer, retrieve their CompanyName, ContactName, and the total number of orders they have placed. Only include customers whose total order count is above the average number of orders per customer across all customers.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-frequency buyers for a new loyalty rewards program. Specifically, they need a list of customers who order more frequently than the typical customer, so the sales team can prioritize outreach and tailor incentive packages.
reference_sql: SELECT c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, c.ContactName, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS TotalOrders FROM Customers c JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, c.ContactName HAVING COUNT(o.OrderID) > (SELECT AVG(OrderCount) FROM (SELECT COUNT(OrderID) AS OrderCount FROM Orders GROUP BY CustomerID) AS AvgOrders)

question: For each customer, retrieve their CompanyName, ContactName, and the total number of orders they have placed. Only include customers whose total order count is greater than the average number of orders placed per customer across all customers.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-frequency buyers to target with a new loyalty rewards program. She needs a list of customers who order more often than the typical customer so the team can prioritize outreach for the VIP tier.
reference_sql: SELECT c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, c.ContactName, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS TotalOrders FROM Customers c JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, c.ContactName HAVING COUNT(o.OrderID) > ( SELECT AVG(OrderCount) FROM ( SELECT COUNT(OrderID) AS OrderCount FROM Orders GROUP BY CustomerID ) AS AvgOrders )

question: For each customer, find their single most expensive order (by total order value after discounts), and then determine whether that order's value exceeds the average order value across ALL of that customer's orders. Return the CustomerID, CompanyName, the OrderID of their most expensive order, the value of that order, the customer's average order value, and a flag ('Above Average' or 'At or Below Average') indicating whether the most expensive order exceeds their own average.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to identify high-value customers whose peak orders significantly outperform their typical spending — a signal for upsell and loyalty program targeting. She needs a report showing each customer's best order compared to their own historical average, so the sales team can prioritize outreach for the upcoming quarter.
reference_sql:
WITH OrderValues AS (
    SELECT
        o.OrderID,
        o.CustomerID,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS OrderTotal
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
    GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.CustomerID
),
CustomerAvg AS (
    SELECT
        CustomerID,
        AVG(OrderTotal) AS AvgOrderValue
    FROM OrderValues
    GROUP BY CustomerID
),
TopOrders AS (
    SELECT
        ov.CustomerID,
        ov.OrderID,
        ov.OrderTotal,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ov.CustomerID ORDER BY ov.OrderTotal DESC) AS rn
    FROM OrderValues ov
)
SELECT
    t.CustomerID,
    c.CompanyName,
    t.OrderID,
    ROUND(t.OrderTotal, 2) AS TopOrderValue,
    ROUND(ca.AvgOrderValue, 2) AS AvgOrderValue,
    CASE
        WHEN t.OrderTotal > (SELECT AVG(ov2.OrderTotal) FROM OrderValues ov2 WHERE ov2.CustomerID = t.CustomerID)
        THEN 'Above Average'
        ELSE 'At or Below Average'
    END AS PerformanceFlag
FROM TopOrders t
JOIN Customers c ON t.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
JOIN CustomerAvg ca ON t.CustomerID = ca.CustomerID
JOIN OrderValues ov ON t.OrderID = ov.OrderID
WHERE t.rn = 1
ORDER BY t.OrderTotal DESC

question: For each customer, find their most recent order and calculate the total revenue (sum of UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) for that order. Return the CustomerID, CompanyName, the most recent OrderID, the OrderDate, and the total revenue of that most recent order. Only include customers who have placed at least 3 orders. Order results by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Sales wants to understand the last purchasing behavior of our most engaged customers. She needs to see what high-frequency buyers (those with 3+ orders) spent on their most recent transaction to identify which accounts may need a follow-up call or upsell opportunity.
reference_sql: WITH CustomerOrderCounts AS ( SELECT CustomerID FROM Orders GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(OrderID) >= 3 ), MostRecentOrders AS ( SELECT o.CustomerID, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate FROM Orders o WHERE o.OrderDate = ( SELECT MAX(o2.OrderDate) FROM Orders o2 WHERE o2.CustomerID = o.CustomerID ) AND o.CustomerID IN (SELECT CustomerID FROM CustomerOrderCounts) ), OrderRevenue AS ( SELECT od.OrderID, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS TotalRevenue FROM "Order Details" od GROUP BY od.OrderID ) SELECT c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName, mro.OrderID, mro.OrderDate, ROUND(orv.TotalRevenue, 2) AS TotalRevenue FROM MostRecentOrders mro JOIN Customers c ON c.CustomerID = mro.CustomerID JOIN OrderRevenue orv ON orv.OrderID = mro.OrderID ORDER BY orv.TotalRevenue DESC

question: For each customer, find their single most recent order and calculate the total revenue from that order (sum of UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount) across all line items). Return the customer's CompanyName, the OrderID of their most recent order, the OrderDate, and the total revenue from that order. Only include customers who have placed at least 2 orders. Order results by total revenue descending.
business_context: The VP of Sales wants to understand what our highest-value 'last touches' look like — specifically, how much revenue each active customer generated on their most recent transaction. This will help the sales team prioritize re-engagement outreach and identify customers whose last order was unusually large or small compared to their historical pattern.
reference_sql:
SELECT
    c.CompanyName,
    o.OrderID,
    o.OrderDate,
    ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS LastOrderRevenue
FROM Customers c
JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
JOIN "Order Details" od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
WHERE o.OrderDate = (
    SELECT MAX(o2.OrderDate)
    FROM Orders o2
    WHERE o2.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
)
AND (
    SELECT COUNT(*)
    FROM Orders o3
    WHERE o3.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
) >= 2
GROUP BY c.CompanyName, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate
ORDER BY LastOrderRevenue DESC;

question: Find the total number of invoices and the total revenue generated, grouped by billing country. Order the results by total revenue in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants a high-level summary of sales performance across all countries. She needs to know which countries are driving the most revenue so the marketing team can prioritize regional campaigns.
reference_sql: SELECT BillingCountry, COUNT(InvoiceId) AS TotalInvoices, SUM(Total) AS TotalRevenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC;

question: Find the total number of invoices and the overall revenue generated, grouped by billing country. Return the billing country, invoice count, and total revenue, ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants a quick summary of sales performance by country to identify the top-performing markets. This will inform decisions about where to focus upcoming marketing campaigns and regional promotions.
reference_sql: SELECT BillingCountry, COUNT(InvoiceId) AS InvoiceCount, SUM(Total) AS TotalRevenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC

question: Find the total number of invoices and the overall revenue generated, grouped by billing country. Order the results by total revenue in descending order.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants a quick summary of how different countries contribute to overall sales. She needs to know both the volume of transactions and the total dollars brought in from each country to prioritize regional marketing spend.

question: For each billing country, calculate the total number of invoices, the total revenue generated, the average invoice value, and the maximum single invoice amount. Only include countries that have placed more than 5 invoices. Order the results by total revenue descending.

question: For each billing country, calculate the total revenue, number of invoices, average invoice value, and the percentage contribution of that country's revenue to the overall global revenue. Only include countries where the average invoice value exceeds the global average invoice value. Order the results by total revenue descending.
business_context: The VP of Global Sales wants to identify high-value markets for a targeted premium subscription campaign. She needs to know which countries not only generate strong total revenue but also have customers whose average spend per invoice is above the global norm, along with each country's share of worldwide revenue.
reference_sql:
WITH global_stats AS (
    SELECT
        AVG(Total) AS global_avg_invoice,
        SUM(Total) AS global_total_revenue
    FROM Invoice
)
SELECT
    i.BillingCountry,
    COUNT(i.InvoiceId) AS num_invoices,
    SUM(i.Total) AS total_revenue,
    AVG(i.Total) AS avg_invoice_value,
    ROUND(SUM(i.Total) * 100.0 / g.global_total_revenue, 2) AS pct_of_global_revenue
FROM Invoice i
CROSS JOIN global_stats g
GROUP BY i.BillingCountry, g.global_total_revenue, g.global_avg_invoice
HAVING AVG(i.Total) > g.global_avg_invoice
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

question: For each billing country, calculate the total revenue, number of invoices, average invoice value, and the percentage contribution of that country's revenue to the overall global revenue. business_context: The VP of International Sales wants to identify high-value markets for targeted expansion. WITH global_stats AS (
    SELECT
        AVG(Total) AS global_avg_invoice,
        SUM(Total) AS global_total_revenue
    FROM Invoice
)
SELECT
    i.BillingCountry,
    COUNT(i.InvoiceId) AS number_of_invoices,
    SUM(i.Total) AS total_revenue,

question: Using only the Invoice table, calculate the following metrics per billing country: total revenue, number of invoices, average invoice value, minimum invoice value, maximum invoice value, and the revenue contribution (as a percentage of global total revenue rounded to 2 decimal places). Return only countries where the average invoice value exceeds the global average invoice value, ordered by total revenue descending.
business_context: The VP of International Sales wants a self-contained revenue performance report by country to identify high-value markets. She specifically wants to focus on countries that are performing above the global average invoice value, so the team can prioritize expansion efforts and allocate regional marketing budgets effectively.
reference_sql:
WITH global_stats AS (
    SELECT
        AVG(Total) AS global_avg,
        SUM(Total) AS global_total
    FROM Invoice
)
SELECT
    i.BillingCountry,
    COUNT(i.InvoiceId)                                        AS invoice_count,
    SUM(i.Total)                                              AS total_revenue,
    ROUND(AVG(i.Total), 2)                                    AS avg_invoice_value,
    MIN(i.Total)                                              AS min_invoice_value,
    MAX(i.Total)                                              AS max_invoice_value,
    ROUND(SUM(i.Total) * 100.0 / g.global_total, 2)          AS revenue_pct_of_global
FROM Invoice i
CROSS JOIN global_stats g
GROUP BY i.BillingCountry, g.global_avg, g.global_total
HAVING AVG(i.Total) > g.global_avg
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC

question: Identify artists whose catalog has been purchased across at least 5 distinct countries, and for whom the average revenue per invoice line exceeds $1.00. For each qualifying artist, return their name, the number of distinct countries that have purchased their tracks, the total number of tracks sold, and the average revenue per invoice line rounded to 2 decimal places. Order results by total tracks sold descending.
business_context: The Head of Global Catalog Strategy wants to pinpoint artists with broad international appeal and strong per-unit monetization. This analysis will inform which artists should receive premium placement and targeted marketing campaigns in underperforming regions.
reference_sql:
WITH artist_sales AS (
    SELECT
        ar.ArtistId,
        ar.Name AS ArtistName,
        COUNT(DISTINCT c.Country) AS distinct_countries,
        SUM(il.Quantity) AS total_tracks_sold,
        AVG(il.UnitPrice) AS avg_revenue_per_line
    FROM Artist ar
    JOIN Album al ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId
    JOIN Track t ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
    JOIN InvoiceLine il ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
    JOIN Invoice i ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
    JOIN Customer c ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
    GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.Country) >= 5
       AND AVG(il.UnitPrice) > 1.00
)
SELECT
    ArtistName,
    distinct_countries,
    total_tracks_sold,
    ROUND(avg_revenue_per_line, 2) AS avg_revenue_per_line
FROM artist_sales
ORDER BY total_tracks_sold DESC;

question: Identify artists whose total revenue exceeds $10, but only considering albums that have been purchased at least 5 times (i.e., appear in at least 5 invoice lines). For each qualifying artist, return their name, the number of distinct qualifying albums, the total number of tracks sold across those albums, and the total revenue generated. Order the results by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of Revenue wants to spotlight high-performing artists whose catalog shows both popularity (albums purchased frequently) and strong monetization. This analysis will inform upcoming partnership and promotional investment decisions for Q3.
reference_sql:
WITH album_purchase_counts AS (
    SELECT
        t.AlbumId,
        COUNT(il.InvoiceLineId) AS purchase_count
    FROM InvoiceLine il
    JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
    GROUP BY t.AlbumId
    HAVING COUNT(il.InvoiceLineId) >= 5
),
qualifying_sales AS (
    SELECT
        t.AlbumId,
        al.ArtistId,
        il.InvoiceLineId,
        il.Quantity,
        il.UnitPrice
    FROM InvoiceLine il
    JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
    JOIN album_purchase_counts apc ON t.AlbumId = apc.AlbumId
    JOIN Album al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
)
SELECT
    ar.Name AS ArtistName,
    COUNT(DISTINCT qs.AlbumId) AS QualifyingAlbumCount,
    SUM(qs.Quantity) AS TotalTracksSold,
    ROUND(SUM(qs.Quantity * qs.UnitPrice), 2) AS TotalRevenue
FROM qualifying_sales qs
JOIN Artist ar ON qs.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
HAVING SUM(qs.Quantity * qs.UnitPrice) > 10
ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC;

question: Identify artists whose catalog has been purchased across at least 5 distinct countries, and where the total revenue generated from their tracks exceeds $100. For each qualifying artist, return their name, the number of distinct countries they've sold to, the total number of distinct albums purchased, and their total revenue. Order the results by total revenue descending.
business_context: The Head of International Sales wants to pinpoint globally resonant artists who drive meaningful revenue across multiple markets. This analysis will inform a targeted international marketing campaign and help prioritize licensing negotiations with high-performing artists.
reference_sql:
WITH artist_sales AS (
    SELECT
        ar.ArtistId,
        ar.Name AS ArtistName,
        i.BillingCountry,
        al.AlbumId,
        il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity AS LineRevenue
    FROM Artist ar
    JOIN Album al ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId
    JOIN Track t ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
    JOIN InvoiceLine il ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
    JOIN Invoice i ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
)
SELECT
    ArtistName,
    COUNT(DISTINCT BillingCountry) AS distinct_countries,
    COUNT(DISTINCT AlbumId) AS distinct_albums_purchased,
    ROUND(SUM(LineRevenue), 2) AS total_revenue
FROM artist_sales
GROUP BY ArtistId, ArtistName
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT BillingCountry) >= 5
   AND SUM(LineRevenue) > 100
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
